title: Ship a fast reflaxe.ocaml authoring and inspection workflow
description: Give application, library, binding, adapter, target, and native-plugin authors one coherent workflow for scaffolding, focused rebuilds, semantic inspection, testing, diagnosis, packaging, and performance. Make the ordinary reflaxe.ocaml edit loop independent of broad hxhx rebuilds, bootstrap regeneration, and every-backend gates.
design: Expose a target-oriented command group in bounded phases. Reuse the typed lowered, runtime, dependency, binding, export, and plugin manifests owned by their architecture Beads instead of scraping generated text. Keep checked-in user and adapter sources separate from generated inspectable files and build caches. Watch mode regenerates only affected OCaml units and invokes focused Dune work. Doctor and inspect commands explain toolchain compatibility and semantic decisions. M22.11 owns plugin-SDK-specific scaffolding and docs; this Bead owns the broader standalone reflaxe.ocaml workflow and shares commands/contracts rather than duplicating them.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Scaffolds exist for an application, library, binding, adapter, and, when M22 is ready, native plugin or target. 2) A warm one-file change regenerates only affected OCaml units and runs a focused Dune build/test without rebuilding hxhx or bootstrap snapshots. 3) Inspect commands expose lowered computations, representation choices, runtime reasons, dependencies, raw/unsafe inventory, and export ABI as those owners land. 4) Binding, adapter, and export commands create, check, update, and explain their typed manifests and rejection diagnostics. 5) Doctor diagnoses Haxe, OCaml, Dune, opam, compiler-libs, runtime manifest, dependency lock, and platform/toolchain compatibility. 6) Cross-host comparison canonicalizes and compares target plans and behavior when the shared target core is available. 7) Packaging supports lock, selected vendoring/offline policy, install, clean reproduction, provenance, and publish preparation. 8) Performance reports separate generation, typecheck/compile, link, load, startup, and runtime with cold/warm/one-file states. 9) Public docs contain runnable commands backed by tests, example coverage follows repo policy, and no support or README readiness is claimed ahead of evidence.
notes: HAXIFY TOOLING REFINEMENT — 2026-07-20. The sibling comparison makes the authoring sequence concrete: resolve the actual package graph; inspect typed interface data read-only; show supported, adapter-required, and rejected declarations; write only on explicit request; compile both the Haxe surface and generated OCaml call sites; then update by semantic diff with handwritten-file collision and stale-output protection. The command names remain intentionally unfrozen. The fast path must cache by interface, package, toolchain, configuration, and generator identity; regenerate affected units only; use focused Dune work; and explain omissions and cache misses. hxhx remains a selected compiler-scale QA/E2E workload, not a per-binding inner-loop dependency. This is within the existing GPT-5.6 review, so no additional Oracle request is warranted.

comments.author: Marcelo Serpa
comments.text: Product-contract clarification 2026-07-18: this Bead owns the quick-iteration leg of the compiler-authoring promise. The supported workflow must make Haxe/Reflaxe pleasant for real compiler work: completion-friendly scaffolds, focused tests, affected-unit regeneration, warm native rebuilds, clear cache-miss explanations, and inspect/doctor commands. Success is measured with cold, warm, and one-file edits and must not hide a full hxhx rebuild, bootstrap regeneration, or broad gate behind the normal author loop. This planning clarification changes no current capability or README readiness.

comments.author: Marcelo Serpa
comments.text:
Implementation start — first bounded authoring slice (2026-07-19)

The first command will be `haxelib run reflaxe.ocaml doctor`. It will distinguish ordinary source generation, native OCaml builds, advanced compiler-libs work, and optional hxhx hosting instead of treating every tool as one all-or-nothing requirement. Human output will lead with practical readiness; `--json` will provide a stable report for CI and future editor tooling.

The doctor will check stock Haxe 4.3.7, Reflaxe 4.x and target package resolution, OCaml, Dune, ocamlfind, opam, compiler-libs, hxhx availability, the current runtime-source layout, project lock/manifest presence, and the exact hosted evidence matrix. Unverified versions will be reported honestly without claiming they are broken; missing required tools will fail. Future semantic runtime and dependency manifests will be named as deferred rather than fabricated from generated text.

This slice does not yet scaffold projects, watch files, introduce a plugin ABI, or claim warm affected-unit regeneration. It establishes the tested diagnostic foundation those workflows can consume. README Goals and North Star progress remain unchanged unless the implemented command proves a broader user-visible readiness change. Because the bead is thinking:high, a written ownership/failure-policy second pass is required before this slice is committed.

comments.author: Marcelo Serpa
comments.text:
Second-pass design review for the bounded doctor slice:

- Ownership remains narrow: the CLI diagnoses the existing environment; it does not install tools, alter projects, select compiler semantics, or claim future plugin/builtin support.
- Read-only behavior is enforced through DoctorProbe and covered by a fake probe. The real probe only executes bounded version/path queries and reads package/project metadata.
- Capability gates fail closed: source requires exact Haxe 4.3.7 plus resolvable Reflaxe/target/runtime sources; native additionally requires compatible ocamlc, ocamlopt, Dune, and findlib; compiler additionally requires compiler-libs; hxhx remains independent and optional for stock-Haxe use.
- Compatible but non-hosted OCaml/Dune versions remain usable warnings and never set verifiedReleaseLane. The future semantic runtime manifest remains an explicit SKIP rather than treating current syntax-derived reports as that contract.
- The package runner is one package-qualified Haxe class shared by development metadata and the source-only archive. CompilerInit bypasses target registration only for the exact HAXELIB_RUN identity, so normal -lib compilation remains unchanged.
- Fast fixtures now enable the package's null-safety rule. The release-shaped proof installs the ZIP into a disposable Haxelib repository, runs the installed JSON doctor with --require native, then compiles, builds, runs, and checks a stock-Haxe external app.
- Oracle/extended review was deliberately skipped: this is a bounded thinking:high diagnostics/package seam backed by official Haxelib/Reflaxe source behavior and executable package evidence, not a scope/release/semantic architecture decision.
- README Goals/North Star progress bars remain unchanged. This improves developer diagnostics but does not itself increase production-readiness claims.

Focused evidence: doctor model/CLI fixtures PASS; source-only package archive fixtures PASS; installed package smoke RO_PACKAGE_INSTALL_SMOKE:PASS with doctorPassed/sourceGenerationReady/nativeBuildReady true and external compile/build/run/stdout all true.

comments.author: Marcelo Serpa
comments.text:
Implementation start — safe incremental authoring loop.

Measured local evidence on the small stock-Haxe native package fixture: clean compile/build 2.67s; unchanged rebuild 1.16s; behavior-preserving one-file change 1.69s. Reflaxe preserved unchanged file mtimes, and the changed run rewrote only WorkReport.ml plus _GeneratedFiles.json before Dune rebuilt and the executable retained exact stdout.

The next bounded command will build on that already-sound behavior. `haxelib run reflaxe.ocaml build` will run a project HXML through a fresh Haxe process, report generation/native wall time, and optionally run a named artifact. `--watch` will use deterministic polling over explicit/discovered Haxe/config/native-source inputs, rerun only after a stable change batch, and recapture the post-build snapshot so generated OCaml never self-triggers a loop. It will not reuse a persistent Haxe server: prior repository evidence found incomplete Reflaxe output under server reuse, so avoiding leaks and nondeterminism is more important than saving the remaining subsecond host startup.

The implementation will keep process execution and file snapshots behind testable boundaries, stream real compiler output, fail closed on missing HXML/commands, stop after failed builds until another input changes, exclude build/cache directories, and offer a bounded max-build count for automation. This slice will not claim semantic affected-module compilation inside Haxe, plugin ABI readiness, or a general daemon. It should prove that the normal loop does not rebuild hxhx or bootstrap snapshots and that unchanged OCaml files remain untouched.

README Goals/North Star bars remain unchanged unless the executable workflow materially changes the stated product readiness. A thinking:high second-pass review will verify polling scope, generated-output feedback prevention, child-process failure behavior, and cross-platform path handling before landing.

comments.author: Marcelo Serpa
comments.text:
Second-pass design review and landing evidence for the safe build/watch slice (2026-07-19):

- User-visible outcome: installed packages now provide `haxelib run reflaxe.ocaml build` and `watch`. Both run the project HXML from its own directory, optionally execute a named artifact, stream child output, publish stable PASS/FAIL markers, and preserve child exit codes.
- Process ownership is intentionally simple: every batch launches and waits for one fresh Haxe child. No daemon, persistent Haxe server, detached process, hxhx rebuild, or bootstrap regeneration is hidden in the ordinary loop. This avoids the previously measured incomplete Reflaxe output under server reuse.
- Haxelib runner state is handled explicitly. The real process host temporarily clears HAXELIB_RUN and HAXELIB_RUN_NAME for child compilation, then restores the original directory and environment on success or failure. This prevents the child compiler from mistaking itself for the package runner and skipping target registration.
- Watch scope is deterministic and bounded to the selected HXML, its bare included HXML files, declared classpaths, common native-source directories, project Dune/package files, and explicit repeated --watch-path inputs. Common output/cache directories are excluded. File inventories are sorted, rapid edits must settle for the debounce interval, roots are rediscovered after HXML edits, and the post-build snapshot becomes the next baseline so generated output cannot self-trigger.
- Failure behavior remains fail closed. Missing projects/HXML/artifacts and malformed numeric options exit 2; compiler and executable failures retain their nonzero codes. Watch mode remains alive after a failed compiler attempt so the next edit can repair it. --max-builds bounds automated proofs by attempts, not successes.
- Cross-platform path handling stays behind haxe.io.Path plus the host boundary. Project-relative paths are resolved from the original invocation directory before haxelib changes the runner working directory; HXML, executable, and explicit watch paths are then resolved from the project root.
- The slice makes no semantic affected-module claim. Reflaxe still types/emits the program through a fresh Haxe process. The measured acceleration is honest: unchanged generated files retain mtimes and Dune reuses its own cache. Local small-fixture measurements were 2.67 s clean, 1.16 s unchanged, and 1.69 s for one behavior-preserving source edit; a real bounded watch rebuilt exactly once after one edit and did not loop.
- Tests isolate process/filesystem/clock behavior through AuthoringHost. Model coverage proves build/run, stable watch batching, child failures, and missing-HXML rejection. CLI coverage proves help and strict numeric/build-limit validation. The real source command compiled/built/ran with exact stdout, and a two-build attached watch detected only src/Main.hx.
- Release-shaped proof installed a newly built source-only ZIP, invoked the installed build command (not direct Haxe), generated and compiled OCaml, ran the executable, and matched stdout. RO_PACKAGE_INSTALL_SMOKE:PASS; archive SHA-256 a6748ee8701e6a115551deb20419364496ee14e45be05135efef9bbf9a6cddd7. Cross-platform receipt aggregation now rejects a consumer that does not prove tooling.buildCommandPassed.
- `npm run test:reflaxe-ocaml:doctor`, package fixtures, production-doc guard, real package install, official formatter, and full `npm run ci:guards` all pass. The final full formatter lane took 74.35 s and was dominated by the already tracked 25,251-line CppTargetCore hotspot; this slice adds no logic there.
- Public package, upstream-Haxe, and production workflow docs now contain runnable build/watch commands and explain the safety/performance boundary. README Goals and North Star bars remain unchanged: this materially improves iteration for the existing advanced-preview route but does not broaden its semantic/platform/plugin readiness claim.
- Oracle escalation was deliberately skipped for this bounded thinking:high process/tooling seam. Existing measured failure evidence made the fresh-process boundary clear, and executable source, installed-package, runtime, and full-guard proofs validate the implementation. The broader architecture Oracle remains authoritative for future semantic inspect/IR work.

The broad bead remains in progress. Application/library/binding/adapter scaffolds, semantic inspection, binding/export commands, packaging ergonomics, and shared-target-core comparison remain subsequent vertical slices.

comments.author: Marcelo Serpa
comments.text:
Implementation start — runnable application and library scaffolds (2026-07-19):

The next bounded slice will add `haxelib run reflaxe.ocaml new app <directory>` and `new library <directory>`. Templates will be tracked package assets, copied transactionally into a new directory, customized with a validated project name, and refused when the destination already exists. Generated READMEs will use the tested doctor/build/watch commands and explain exactly which artifact is produced.

The inventory found one concrete library blocker: `ocaml_dune_layout=lib` emits a valid Dune library, but the post-emit build helper always requests an executable target. The slice will teach that existing helper to build the library project with Dune `@all`, and will reject run requests for a library layout. This is target build tooling, not a new ABI or semantic lowering path.

Application scaffolds must compile, build, run, and print the documented output. Library scaffolds must emit a library-only Dune project and complete a real native Dune build without generating an executable stanza. The source-checkout fixture and isolated installed-package proof will both exercise generated projects; package receipts will record that scaffolding itself passed.

Binding and handwritten-adapter scaffolds are intentionally not generated in this slice. The current target has no structured native-source/dependency manifest or typed interface-import contract, so copying an `.ml` file beside generated output would give users a fragile and misleading project. Requests for those kinds will fail before creating files and name the typed binding/adapter work as the prerequisite. Native plugin/target scaffolding remains owned by M22.11 and will not be duplicated here.

This remains thinking:high because it changes distributed tooling and the Dune target contract. A written second pass will review transactional output, package-root versus invocation-root handling, name/path validation, installed archive contents, library run rejection, and release-claim wording before landing. README Goals and North Star bars should remain unchanged unless the runnable installed proof materially broadens the supported product claim.

comments.author: Marcelo Serpa
comments.text:
Second-pass design review and landing evidence for runnable scaffolds (2026-07-19):

- User-visible outcome: installed packages now provide `haxelib run reflaxe.ocaml new app <directory>` and `new library <directory>`. The generated app builds and runs with documented output; the generated Haxe library emits a library-only Dune project and builds a native `.cmxa`.
- Project creation is all-or-nothing. The tool validates the kind, destination, parent, project name, package boundary, template inventory, and every placeholder before writing. It writes a sibling staging directory and atomically renames it into place. Existing destinations and stale transactions are rejected, and failed writes clean their staging tree rather than leaving a partial project.
- Package-root and invocation-root ownership remain separate. Relative destinations are resolved from the user's original directory even when Haxelib changes the runner directory. The destination parent is canonicalized before the package-boundary check, which also handles symlinked parents; Windows comparison is case-insensitive. Scaffold templates are trusted, tracked package assets, collected and emitted in deterministic sorted order.
- Names are restricted to a beginner-readable, interpolation-safe ASCII set and converted into a stable lowercase package slug. Unknown template placeholders fail before a destination is created. User files are never reopened or overwritten on a repeated command.
- The library build correction is narrow: `ocaml_dune_layout=lib|library` selects Dune `@all`, which builds every library module without inventing an executable target. `ocaml_run` now fails before native compilation with an actionable library-layout diagnostic. Executable layouts retain their previous named `.exe`/`.bc` targets and CMI handling.

comments.author: Marcelo Serpa
comments.text:
Implementation start — truthful compiler-owned artifact inspection (2026-07-19):

The next bounded command will be `haxelib run reflaxe.ocaml inspect`. It will read the completed build artifacts that the current target already owns: Reflaxe's generated-file receipt, the profile report, the current runtime-selection report, and the optional typed OCaml place-lowering report. Human output will lead with the active profile, emitted-file count, selected runtime modules/reasons, and lowered place operations. `--json` will expose a stable schema for CI and editor tooling.

The command will validate exact current schemas and fail on malformed or stale required reports. The output directory is project-relative and read-only. Missing typed-place data is a truthful not-enabled state by default, with an explicit `--require-lowering` gate for workflows that need it; users will be told to compile with `-D ocaml_lowering_report`.

This slice will not scan generated OCaml or Dune text to invent semantic facts. The runtime report will be labeled as the current compiler/syntax-derived selection report, not the future locked semantic runtime manifest. Program-wide representation, native dependency, raw/unsafe, binding, and curated export-ABI inspection will remain explicit unavailable capabilities until their owning typed manifests land. The place report will be described narrowly as the migrated assignment/update family, not a whole-program IR.

Focused proof will compile a real place-assignment fixture with the current target, inspect its generated reports, verify source/carrier/representation/effect/schedule/runtime-requirement summaries, then cover human rendering, missing optional lowering, `--require-lowering`, malformed schema, and missing output. The isolated installed-package proof and cross-platform receipt contract will also require a successful inspect command.

This remains `thinking:high` because the CLI schema must not overstate semantic authority. A written second pass will review authority labels, schema/failure behavior, source-path handling, installed-package output, and deferred-capability wording before landing. README Goals and North Star bars remain unchanged unless inspection itself materially broadens production readiness.

comments.text:
Second-pass design review and landing evidence for compiler-owned inspection (2026-07-19):

- User-visible outcome: installed packages now provide `haxelib run reflaxe.ocaml inspect`, with concise human output and schema-v1 JSON. It explains emitted files, the active compile profile, current runtime module selection/reasons, and the optional typed place assignment/update plans already owned by core lowering.
- Authority is explicit. The command reads only `_GeneratedFiles.json`, `ocaml_profile_report.json`, `ocaml_runtime_plan_report.json`, and optional `ocaml_lowering_report.json`. It never scans generated OCaml or Dune text, selects runtime helpers, reconstructs representations, or changes a project. The runtime report says `semanticManifest: false`; the place report identifies its assignment/update-family scope and says it is not a whole-program IR.
- Required current report schemas fail closed: generated receipt v1, profile v2, and runtime selection v2. Typed place lowering v4 is optional by default and records whether it was required. `--require-lowering` now renders a missing report as an explicit failure instead of a skip and names the HXML define needed to produce it.
- Completed-output validation goes beyond JSON parsing. Generated receipt paths must be safe, unique relative paths and must exist. Selected runtime module names must be safe, copied `.ml`/`.mli` sources must exist, and each selected module must have exactly one non-empty inclusion-reason entry. Profile/runtime profile and mode must agree. Lowered plans require the expected model, sha256 revision, count, semantic/carrier/representation facts, source byte offsets, effect schedule, and runtime requirement IDs.
- The summary uses `valid/invalid`, not `ready/not ready`. A valid inspection proves these compiler artifacts are internally consistent; it does not claim a native executable was built, the target is production-ready, or any deferred product scope has closed.
- Program-wide representation, source-rooted semantic runtime requirements, structured native dependencies, raw/Obj.magic proofs, typed `.mli` bindings, and curated public export ABI remain machine-readable `unavailable` entries. Their future schema readers must stay with their semantic owners and contribute typed summaries rather than making this CLI a new inference mega-file.
- Output and project paths are resolved from the caller's project, so the same command works through Haxelib's changed runner directory. Inspection is read-only, accepts an explicit output directory, emits JSON even on artifact-invalid failures, preserves exit 2 for CLI/project usage errors, and emits exit 1 for invalid or missing required artifacts.
- A real current-target fixture produces and inspects 14 sealed static-place plans. It verifies semantic `Int` to OCaml `int`, ref-cell representation reasons, source byte offsets, effect order, and runtime requirement IDs. Negative coverage proves optional/required lowering behavior, schema rejection, unsafe generated paths, missing runtime sources, cross-report profile disagreement, missing output, and bad options.

The isolated installed source-only ZIP creates/builds/runs a starter, inspects it with required lowering, and records `tooling.inspectCommandPassed`; the Linux/macOS receipt aggregator rejects a missing proof. Final package SHA-256: 68e2adc7a8eb79425f571052959dfc1ce4ab99dbe0143c1b1ca22b9ab180f1b4.

The review then changed only readiness wording/state and the required-lowering label; all affected doctor/authoring/scaffold/inspect, package archive/matrix, production-doc, installed-package, syntax, and official formatting checks were rerun and passed on the final state. The final 764-file formatter took 96.908 seconds, again dominated by the pre-existing 25,251-line CppTargetCore shard; this slice adds no logic there.

- README Goals and North Star progress bars remain unchanged. Inspection makes the existing advanced-preview workflow easier to understand but does not broaden semantic, runtime-manifest, ABI, binding, plugin, or platform readiness.

comments.author: Marcelo Serpa
comments.text:
HAXE-SERVER ASSUMPTION CORRECTION — 2026-07-19

The prior statement that persistent Haxe-server reuse inherently produced incomplete Reflaxe output was too broad. The controlled failure combined a cached delta request with a deleted target-output directory: Haxe reported four recompiled modules, so Reflaxe correctly lacked Main.ml. When a complete revision-matched output set was preserved, unchanged and one-file-change server requests built and ran correctly, including changed build-macro behavior.

The current fresh-process watcher remains the supported safe path. A future persistent-server option may materially reduce the roughly 1.10-second outside-target cost measured on hosted Linux, but it first needs an explicit full-snapshot-plus-delta protocol, program/output revision key, reset/cancellation contract, deterministic failure when output is missing or stale, and proof that no macro/plugin/target state leaks. haxe_ocaml-7201t and its superseding GPT-5.6 package own that lifecycle decision. This correction adds no supported server mode or readiness change.

title: Generate curated OCaml export ABIs for Haxe libraries
description: Let a Haxe-authored library explicitly publish a stable OCaml-facing API without exposing private generated records, boxes, dispatch structures, or runtime details. Generate checked adapter modules and a curated mli, then prove the package from an independent OCaml consumer.
design: Exports are opt-in through annotations or a package manifest. The export planner chooses boundary-specific public representations and explicit conversions independently of internal optimization carriers. It generates adapter implementation and curated interface artifacts, checks the implementation against that interface, records a semantic ABI version and toolchain key, and compares releases. ocamlc -i remains an inspection tool rather than the public contract.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Explicit export selection produces deterministic adapter modules and a curated mli. 2) Public representations and conversions are stable and separate from internal carriers. 3) Private class records, Dynamic boxes, dispatch structures, runtime modules, and unsafe casts do not leak into the interface. 4) An independent OCaml project compiles and executes against an exported Haxe library. 5) ABI diff checks detect compatible and breaking changes and bind the contract to the declared OCaml/toolchain range. 6) Internal representation changes can preserve the public interface. 7) Missing, stale, incompatible, or unsafe export plans fail before packaging. 8) Docs, examples, package provenance, performance, and README/North Star product scope are updated only for proven support.

title: Productize typed OCaml imports, adapters, and native dependencies
description: Provide a reproducible typed path from OCaml interfaces and packages into Haxe. Import representable first-order interfaces exactly, route advanced OCaml features through small typed ml/mli adapters, and reject interfaces that cannot be represented safely instead of widening them to Dynamic.
design: Use a toolchain-pinned typed OCaml interface reader over mli, cmi, or cmti rather than regex or ocamlc -i text. Record interface, toolchain, package, module, generated-name, supported/adapted/rejected-feature, source, digest, platform, profile, ownership, and license facts. Render Dune and opam files from structured dependency/source manifests. Adapters are ordinary typed native units with explicit mli boundaries, not raw code.
acceptance_criteria: 1) A capability matrix classifies exact binding, typed adapter, and deterministic rejection. 2) Values, ordinary functions, labels, optionals, tuples, records, closed variants, exceptions, opaque types, callbacks, and first-order generics have positive imports. 3) Functor or other advanced capability works through one small adapter, while GADT, higher-rank, first-class module, or other unrepresentable fixtures reject with an actionable next-level diagnostic. 4) Unsupported types never widen to Dynamic or untyped Obj.t. 5) Interface, package, toolchain, source, name-map, digest, profile, platform, ownership, and license manifests are deterministic and tamper checked. 6) Dune and opam outputs render from structured data and one nontrivial external package builds in a clean environment. 7) Adapter and raw authority remain distinct, completion and source mapping are tested, and README/North Star product scope is updated only when supported.
notes: SIBLING-TARGET COMPARISON — 2026-07-20. Read-only review of haxe.ruby, haxe.elixir.codex, haxe.rust, and haxe.go confirms the accepted GPT-5.6 direction and adds concrete acceptance detail. The stable OCaml path should pair an exact low-level ocaml.* facade with an optional ergonomic Haxe wrapper; keep portable Haxe std semantics separate; discover typed native interfaces before writing files; generate declarations precisely or omit them with a reason; keep opam/Dune as dependency owners through a structured lock; use manifest-owned ml/mli adapter islands for functors, GADTs, compiler-libs, lifetimes, or other contracts Haxe cannot express; and reject unsupported stable bindings rather than widening them to Dynamic. Acceptance should include one ordinary external opam package, one compiler-libs or compiler-internals surface, one advanced adapter, deterministic upgrade/downgrade diffing, collision/stale-file failures, and a small runtime call through the real package. No new Oracle review is needed: the existing GPT-5.6 native-power review already covers this exact architecture and remains the thinking:xhigh second pass.

comments.author: Marcelo Serpa
comments.text: Product-contract clarification 2026-07-18: this Bead owns the OCaml-ecosystem leg of the compiler-authoring promise. In addition to a nontrivial ordinary package, acceptance evidence should include an appropriate compiler-libs or compiler-internals surface: exact typed bindings where Haxe can represent it, or a small checked ml/mli adapter where it cannot. The goal is deep practical access without pretending Haxe has the full OCaml type system; raw injection remains an explicit last resort. This planning clarification changes no current capability or README readiness.

title: Make reflaxe.ocaml runtime requirements semantic and fail closed
description: Record why Haxe semantics need runtime support when lowering makes the decision, then package a checked dependency closure. Keep the current structured target-AST scan as a consistency check, but stop using rendered names as semantic authority and stop silently discarding unknown requested modules.
design: Introduce stable semantic runtime requirement records and a locked capability-to-feature-to-source manifest with transitive dependencies, versions, hashes, profiles, and licenses. Seed the ledger through the first lowered place/evaluation family and expand by bounded capability. Portable-full may remain explicit during transition while reporting actual roots. Portable-selective must prove completeness, and metal never falls back to portable, raw, or unchecked unsafe behavior.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Unknown requested, missing, stale, modified, or profile-illegal runtime modules fail deterministically. 2) Each admitted runtime root names its source identity, semantic capability, causing representation or lowering decision, profile, implementation feature, and transitive dependencies. 3) A locked manifest owns runtime module closure, hashes, versions, and licenses. 4) Every generated internal runtime reference is explained by a planned requirement or explicit compiler infrastructure declaration, and every plan is checked against target syntax. 5) Raw fragments and adapters declare their own requirements. 6) Runtime-free, selective, explicit-full, metal-positive, metal-negative, missing-file, changed-hash, unknown-module, and opaque-raw fixtures pass. 7) Runtime reports show the complete source-to-module reason chain. 8) Syntax or token scanning is no longer required for correctness; README/North Star and release-scope impact are recorded.

That wording can overstate evidence: a recorded HxArray assignment requirement does not prove every HxArray call, type annotation, generated helper, or conversion has its own explanation. Before adding another partial family, this slice will bump only the runtime-requirement report schema and replace explained/unexplained module labels with exact overlap labels: compiler-observed modules with a recorded requirement root, and compiler-observed modules without one. comments.author: Marcelo Serpa
comments.text: CHECKPOINT — Runtime requirement report schema 3 now describes exactly what the compiler can prove. Schema 2 called a whole runtime module explained when any recorded reason selected that module. That was too broad: HxArray, for example, is used by many compiler paths beyond the migrated assignment/update family. Schema 3 removes the explainedCompilerObservedModules and unexplainedCompilerObservedModules fields. It records compilerObservationGranularity as module-name-only, then partitions observed names into compilerObservedModulesWithRequirementRoots and compilerObservedModulesWithoutRequirementRoots. A requirement root means the first helper module directly selected by a recorded compiler reason. Name overlap is now explicitly not evidence that every generated use site is explained. comments.text: DEPENDENCY CHECKPOINT — The four remaining module-name gaps are not equivalent to the completed typed-extern families. title: Represent OCaml control effects before target syntax
description: Represent return, break, continue, Haxe throw, and their target identities in the typed OCaml-lowered model before selecting OCaml expression or private-exception syntax. Preserve arbitrary Haxe thrown values and prevent compiler control mechanisms from colliding with user exceptions.
design: Use structured expression lowering by default. Each control transfer records kind, target identity, payload semantic and carrier type, effects, source origin, and selected target mechanism. A scoped private exception is an implementation choice, not source semantics. Do not introduce a broad CFG because loops or exceptions exist. Reconsider only a bounded function-local block form if repeated fixtures prove that dominance, edge arguments, liveness, or shared cleanup edges are required.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Every admitted return, break, continue, and throw names a valid semantic target and complete payload conversion. 2) Nested loop, closure, return, throw, catch, and arbitrary-value exception fixtures match upstream Haxe behavior. 3) Compiler control exceptions cannot be caught by user handlers or leak through exported APIs. 4) Unsupported control shapes fail before target syntax. 5) Admitted old builder branches are removed after hard cutover. 6) Lowered dumps, validator negatives, OCaml typecheck, native execution, profile, and determinism tests pass. 7) No broad CFG is added unless the documented evidence threshold is met and a new xhigh decision approves it. 8) README/North Star and mega-file impact are recorded.

title: Lower OCaml calls and conversions through one typed contract
description: Make direct calls, closures, dynamic dispatch, intrinsics, runtime helpers, OCaml externs, and typed adapters consume one selected call and conversion contract before OcamlExpr construction. Preserve labelled and optional arguments, including omitted versus explicit option values, and reject unsupported native boundaries deterministically.
design: Add typed call and conversion plans referenced by the small OCaml-lowered model. Record exact callable identity, call kind, labels, optionality, receiver and argument evaluation schedule, semantic and carrier types, conversions, result, effects, native dependency, and runtime requirement. Keep host typing authoritative and do not recover calls from target names. Do not broaden raw authority or map unsupported boundaries to Dynamic.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Every admitted call has one stable selected kind and complete argument/result conversions. 2) Definition and call-site callable shapes cannot diverge. 3) Labelled arguments, omitted optionals, explicit None or Some values, closures, callbacks, direct calls, dynamic dispatch, intrinsics, runtime helpers, and first typed adapter boundaries have positive and negative fixtures. 4) Required native packages and runtime capabilities are referenced structurally. 5) Unsupported carriers, arities, labels, callbacks, or conversions fail at the Haxe source boundary. 6) The old admitted call/coercion branches are removed in the hard cutover. 7) Lowered dumps, OCaml typecheck, native execution, generated-code shape, profile, and determinism tests pass. 8) No target-name rediscovery, raw fallback, Dynamic widening, or printer semantics are added; README/North Star and mega-file impact are recorded.

title: Unify reflaxe.ocaml representation, storage, and capture decisions
description: Give type mapping, defaults, class and interface layout, locals, mutable captures, assignments, calls, null, Dynamic, and target boundaries one immutable OCaml representation owner. Preserve the difference between Haxe semantic types and OCaml carriers, and make every ref, box, wrapper, dispatch record, null encoding, and unsafe conversion explainable before syntax construction.
design: Build on the first place/evaluation nodes rather than creating independent side tables. Key representation decisions by semantic type plus representation domain, including internal values, mutable or captured storage, Dynamic, native imports, exports, and runtime payloads. Add explicit conversions between domains. Move local storage and capture reasons into typed lowered function plans. OcamlCompiler and OcamlBuilder may consume the registry but may not select conflicting carriers independently. Keep Obj.magic behind reviewed proof records and inventories; do not attempt a big-bang Dynamic or class-layout rewrite.
acceptance_criteria: 1) One documented representation registry has deterministic keys, selected carriers, null/identity/aliasing/mutation policy, reason, profile, and proof. 2) Type mapping, defaults, layout, place storage, local storage, capture, and admitted calls consume the same decisions. 3) Captured-and-mutated locals share one storage identity and ref introduction is reportable. 4) Cross-domain conversions are explicit and identity-preserving values are not silently copied. 5) Obj.magic and Obj.repr or Obj.obj uses in the admitted scope are justified, inventoried, tested, and rejected in disallowed profiles. 6) Conflicting or missing decisions fail in the semantic validator. 7) Focused null, Dynamic, class/interface, generic, local/capture, native-boundary, code-shape, native-execution, and determinism tests pass. 8) OcamlCompiler and OcamlBuilder lose the migrated duplicate selection branches, mega-file impact is recorded, and README/North Star status is reviewed.

comments.text: 2026-07-18 concrete representation seam from the Array<Int> += cutover: upstream Haxe 4.3.7 itself normalizes an effectful compound lvalue into preceding base/index temporaries (confirmed in a pretty typed dump), so the target-owned place node receives local reads rather than the original receiver/index calls. Current reflaxe.ocaml stores the generated base temporary through `let base = Obj.magic (receiver ())`, then the typed array operation consumes it as `int HxArray.t`. Runtime behavior and order are correct and the admitted operation adds no further cast, but the local-storage conversion is outside the place plan. This is direct acceptance evidence for 9bome: the representation registry and lowered function/local-storage plan must assign that Haxe-generated temporary the same Array<Int> carrier and either prove an identity conversion or reject it; the place emitter must not become a second local-storage owner.

comments.author: Marcelo Serpa
comments.text:
SLICE BOUNDARY — local storage and captured mutation

Practical outcome: this first implementation step will not change generated OCaml. It will move the decision about which Haxe locals need an OCaml ref cell out of the 7,600-line syntax builder and into a focused planner that the builder consumes. A ref cell is shared mutable storage; it is required when a closure or nested control-flow region must observe later writes. Straight-line assignments can continue to use ordinary immutable let bindings by introducing a newer binding with the same name.

The planner will preserve the current behavior exactly, including conservative treatment of loops, nested blocks, nested functions, expression-position writes, compound assignment, increment/decrement, and captured-and-mutated locals. It will return typed storage decisions with closed, beginner-readable reason codes and deterministic local-id order. The builder will ask the plan whether a local needs a ref; it will no longer own or duplicate the traversal that makes that decision.

This is migration infrastructure, not the completed representation registry. The first slice intentionally defers carrier/null/boxing choices, weak-polymorphism and Obj.t slot cleanup, persistent cross-build caching, and sealing the storage plan against the final function-body revision. The next slice must attach these decisions to the revisioned lowered-function boundary instead of allowing a permanent unsealed side plan. Existing M2/M3 behavior, the mutability snapshot, native execution, formatting, and mega-file gravity are the acceptance evidence. README and North Star readiness remain unchanged because this is an output-inert ownership improvement.

comments.author: Marcelo Serpa
comments.text:
IMPLEMENTATION SECOND PASS — bounded local-storage extraction

Outcome: Haxe locals that are written now receive a typed OCaml storage decision before their declaration is emitted. The decision says either “use a newer immutable let binding for a straight-line write” or “use one shared ref cell,” and records concrete reasons such as a loop, nested function, captured mutation, compound assignment, or increment/decrement. The syntax builder asks this plan what to emit instead of walking the Haxe expression tree and deciding for itself.

Architecture review: this follows the accepted GPT-5.6 C-lite direction as an output-inert migration step. The planner is request-local, deterministic, closed over the currently supported reason family, and independently tested. The returned plan protects its retained arrays from caller mutation. OcamlBuilder lost the complete 145-line decision traversal and fell from 7,688 lines at HEAD to 7,518 lines; it gained only imports, current-plan plumbing, and plan queries. The current classification intentionally preserves nested-function and conservative nested-expression behavior rather than mixing a semantic change into the ownership move.

Important limit: planning is still invoked while OcamlBuilder enters a function or block, so this is not yet the durable revision-sealed lowered-function boundary required by the full bead. The next slice must build and seal the local-storage plan against the exact final typed body, then expose it through the common function plan. Carrier types, null encoding, weak-polymorphism handling, Obj.t slots, boxes, wrappers, and cross-boundary conversions remain deferred. No completion or readiness claim follows from this slice.

Evidence: the direct macro fixture proves straight-line, compound, increment, expression-position, loop, captured mutation, stable ordering, defensive copies, and duplicate-decision failure. M2 and M3 compile and build native OCaml while retaining mutable-loop and captured-local behavior. The focused mutability golden and the complete snapshot suite are byte-identical. Package-archive fixtures, Q-risk routing, Reflaxe/hxhx boundary, local-path, mega-file, official formatter, and diff checks pass. README Goals and North Star progress remain unchanged.

comments.author: Marcelo Serpa
comments.text:
NEXT SLICE BOUNDARY — revision-sealed function plans

Practical outcome: a function’s local-storage choices will be computed from the exact final typed body and locked to that body before OCaml source generation begins. If a later callback changes the body, code generation will reject the stale plan instead of rescanning a different tree and silently making new choices.

Implementation boundary: generalize the current place-plan registry into one lowered-function registry. One sealed function record will contain the program/function/body/pipeline identity, its admitted place-operation plans, and its immutable local-storage plan. The final Reflaxe preprocessor will compute both from the same body revision. OcamlCompiler will pass that sealed function record to OcamlBuilder; nested blocks and functions will consume it without rescanning. Standalone initializer/expression roots that are not ClassFuncData bodies will receive an explicitly precomputed plan from compiler orchestration, preserving one decision owner without pretending they have a sealed function identity.

The pipeline revision must change because an old cached plan does not contain storage decisions. Existing late-body-mutation and lifecycle tests must prove the new revision fails closed and remains deterministic. Generated .ml behavior should remain byte-identical; lifecycle/report metadata may change only where it truthfully names the new function-plan revision. Carrier/null/boxing representation and public storage reporting remain later slices. README Goals and North Star readiness remain unchanged.

comments.author: Marcelo Serpa
comments.text:
IMPLEMENTATION SECOND PASS — revision-sealed local storage

Practical outcome: the OCaml target now decides local mutable storage from the exact final typed function body, at the same final preprocessing boundary that plans field and array updates. Previously, the syntax builder walked the body again and could make a fresh ref-versus-let choice after planning. Now one sealed function record carries the body identity, its local-storage choices, and its place-operation plans. If a later callback changes the body, source generation rejects the stale record instead of silently rescanning.

Nested functions are covered explicitly. A variable owned by a closure can still use ordinary immutable let rebinding for a straight-line assignment. A write from that closure to an outer captured variable uses the shared ref cell. The direct planner fixture and M3 native source check prove both sides. Standalone field initializers and expression roots receive an explicit precomputed storage plan from compiler orchestration; they do not pretend to be revision-sealed ClassFuncData bodies.

Architecture review: this remains within the accepted GPT-5.6 target-lowered-tree direction. OcamlPlacePlanRegistry and its sealer became the broader OcamlFunctionPlanRegistry and OcamlFunctionPlanSealer instead of creating a second side table. OcamlBuilder consumes the sealed choice and no longer performs block or function storage scans. It is now 7,465 lines, 223 below the 7,688-line inventory baseline. The target pipeline revision changed to ocaml-function-plans-v2 because old cached records do not contain storage decisions. No builder rebinding, fallback path, raw OCaml, Dynamic, Obj.magic recovery, or broad CFG was added.

Evidence on the staged code: the local-storage fixture, M2, M3, lifecycle trace, deterministic repeat, late-body-mutation rejection, complete snapshot suite, package-archive fixtures, Q-risk routing, Reflaxe/hxhx boundary, bridge boundary, no-Dynamic, runtime/stdlib closure audit, local-path, production-doc, mega-file, JavaScript syntax, diff, and official 799-file Haxe formatting checks all pass. The classifier correctly assigns Q3 because central representation files changed; the expensive large-hxhx and authentic-compiler consumer proofs are routed to CI instead of being repeated in the ordinary local loop.

Deferred scope remains substantial: semantic-type-to-OCaml-carrier choices, null and boxing policy, weak-polymorphism and Obj.t slot cleanup, explicit cross-domain conversions, public unsafe inventories, and canonical cross-host local identities. The bead remains open. README Goals and North Star readiness bars remain unchanged because this is an internal correctness and ownership improvement, not a newly supported user capability.

comments.author: Marcelo Serpa
comments.text:
REGRESSION REPAIR — distinguish lexical scope from tree depth

Practical outcome: the two portable programs that failed after local-storage plans were sealed now compile and run again. The repair does not add Obj.magic or widen either array type. It restores the intended storage choice before OCaml source is built.

Cause: the sealed planner walked the complete function once and treated every assignment below the root expression as a nested-block write. That confused expression-tree nesting with lexical scope. In the failing Rest construction, an inner temporary was declared and assigned in the same nested block. The older builder correctly emitted a newer immutable let binding there. The sealed planner instead forced a ref cell, which exposed an existing generic carrier mismatch between Obj.t HxArray.t and int HxArray.t.

Fix: the planner now records the lexical scope where each Haxe local is declared. A plain assignment in that same scope may use immutable rebinding. A nested block that writes a local declared outside the block still receives one shared ref cell. Loops, nested functions, captured mutation, expression-position writes, compound assignments, and increment or decrement retain their conservative ref behavior. The focused fixture proves both sides in one example: an inner local assigned in its declaring block remains immutable, while an outer local written by that block becomes a ref with the nested-block-mutation reason.

Comparison evidence: candidate 781f4236b, before plan sealing, generated an ordinary let for the inner temporary. The repaired sealed path generates that same relevant shape while retaining revision validation. The exact formerly failing fixtures haxe_core_bucket02_basic and haxe_extern_core_basic pass compile, native build, and execution. The full strict portable Tier 1 corpus passes all 75 fixtures with four isolated workers. Local-storage planning, M2, M3, preprocessor lifecycle and late-mutation rejection, snapshot, package archive, official 799-file formatting, QA routing, Reflaxe/hxhx and bridge boundaries, no-Dynamic, runtime closure, mega-file, and diff checks also pass. QA classification is Q2.

Limits: this fixes lexical storage selection only. Generic carrier unification, weak-polymorphism and Obj.t cleanup, null and boxing policy, and explicit cross-domain conversions remain owned by this open bead. Incident portable-storage-carrier-29764683800 stays open until an exact-head hosted Tier 1 successor succeeds. README Goals and North Star bars remain unchanged because this restores an internal compiler invariant rather than adding a user-visible capability.

comments.author: Marcelo Serpa
comments.text:
NEXT SLICE BOUNDARY — seed one program-wide representation registry with exact Int

Practical outcome: the compiler will have one inspectable answer to the narrow question “how is an exact, non-null Haxe Int carried in this OCaml representation domain?” Existing typed place plans and revision-sealed local-storage plans will reference that answer instead of inventing origin-specific representation labels or asking the syntax builder to map the type again.

Scope: introduce a request-local registry keyed by semantic type plus representation domain. Admit exact Int only, with separate internal-value, mutable-storage, captured-storage, instance-field, static-field, and array-element keys as needed by current plans. Each immutable decision records the direct OCaml int carrier, non-null/value/direct-boxing policies, supported profiles, a beginner-readable reason, and a named proof contract. Conflicting decisions and stale program revisions fail before syntax construction.

Hard cutover: existing exact-Int place plans will use registry identities, and mutated exact-Int local declarations inside sealed function bodies will resolve their carrier through the referenced registry decision. Missing references in this admitted subset are compiler errors. Other semantic types and standalone non-function roots remain explicitly unmigrated and keep their current path; this slice does not claim their representation is unified.

Evidence: add direct registry conflict, determinism, defensive-copy, and revision tests; extend local-storage tests for internal, mutable, and captured Int domains; update only intentional lowering-report goldens; require byte-equivalent generated OCaml and existing M2/M3, place, lifecycle, snapshot, package, formatting, architecture, and portable checks. The broader type mapper, null, Dynamic, generics, class/interface layout, calls, conversions, unsafe inventory, and public ABI remain deferred. README Goals and North Star bars should remain unchanged because this is an internal ownership cutover.

comments.author: Marcelo Serpa
comments.text:
IMPLEMENTATION SECOND PASS — exact non-null Int representation registry

Practical outcome: the OCaml target now has one request-local, program-wide answer for how an exact, non-null Haxe Int is stored in each admitted use domain. Ordinary values, mutable locals, captured locals, instance fields, static fields, array elements, and array indices refer to deterministic registry decisions instead of inventing per-expression labels or asking the syntax builder to map Int again. Each decision records the OCaml carrier, null behavior, identity, aliasing, mutation owner, boxing policy, eligible profiles, a plain-language reason, and a named proof.

The proof is deliberately narrow. On the currently tested 64-bit OCaml hosts, every signed 32-bit Haxe Int value fits in OCaml int. That proves storage and pass-through only. Overflow-sensitive and bit-pattern-sensitive operations still use HxInt, and this slice does not admit a 32-bit OCaml target.

Second-pass correction: the first draft still let OcamlBuilder ask whether a mutated Haxe local was exactly Int and reconstruct the expected storage domain. That would have left the emitter as a second policy owner. The sealed function plan now gives every mutated local one closed answer: use this named program decision, or remain explicitly unmigrated with its semantic type recorded. Syntax construction follows that answer and fails if the function plan, semantic type, representation domain, registry identity, or program revision disagrees. Field and array plans likewise validate semantic type, carrier, and domain before output.

Inspection now reports schema 4 with the exact-non-null-int-v1 representation scope. The lowering artifact records schema 7 and validates that every admitted place and array-index reference resolves to the matching program decision. Missing and wrong-domain decisions fail in focused negative tests. The four intentional lowering goldens changed only to replace expression-local representation labels with shared decisions and their proof; generated OCaml source behavior remains unchanged.

Evidence on the final implementation: direct representation and local-storage fixtures pass; M2 and M3 native builds pass; inspection and its missing/wrong-domain negatives pass; lifecycle and late-body-mutation rejection pass; all four deterministic place-report fixtures pass compile/build/run; all snapshots are byte-equivalent; all 75 portable fixtures compile, build, run, and match behavior, including Int32, Float/nullable, Dynamic, null, interface, reflection, macro, stdlib, IO, network, and threading controls. Package archive, production docs, runtime/stdlib closure, no-Dynamic, bridge and Reflaxe/hxhx core boundaries, QA routing, local paths, mega-file gravity, diff checks, and the official 799-file formatter pass.

Mega-file review: OcamlBuilder is 7,514 lines versus the 7,688-line inventory baseline, a net reduction of 174 lines. New selection and validation live in focused lowered modules. OcamlCompiler is 3,705 lines and receives only registry lifecycle/wiring in this slice; its broader growth remains separate debt.

Deferred scope remains substantial: nullable and Dynamic representation, arrays as values, classes/interfaces and layout, generics, weak-polymorphism and Obj.t slots, explicit cross-domain conversions, calls, imports/adapters, exports, unsafe inventories, public ABI, and shared stock-Haxe/hxhx target input. This bead remains open. README Goals and North Star bars remain unchanged because this is an internal ownership and validation cutover, not a newly supported user capability.

comments.author: Marcelo Serpa
comments.text:
FINAL-REVIEW NOTE — deterministic report identity and serialized native checks

The last mechanical validator cleanup changed only the programRevision values embedded in the four lowering goldens. After removing those revision fields, the expected and actual reports are identical, and running the same candidate twice produces the same new revision. Generated OCaml and runtime behavior are unchanged.

Investigation found a separate Reflaxe framework limitation: ProgramRevision currently hashes Haxe's printed typed-expression form. That form can include compiler-local numbering, so an irrelevant refactor inside target or macro code may change a user-program revision even when the normalized user program does not. New bug haxe_ocaml-9s7fk owns a target-neutral fix in the fullofcaffeine/reflaxe fork. It keeps host-program identity separate from target-pipeline identity and is related to the future stock-Haxe/hxhx stable-ID envelope. This limitation does not make a stale plan valid or nondeterministic within the current build, so it does not block this exact-Int cutover.

The four native place fixtures are now run serially in the final local check. A four-worker retry caused Dune/output cleanup contention and one killed executable; each fixture then passed compile, native build, execution, and report comparison alone. Parallelization is therefore intentionally avoided for this focused rerun. The full 75-fixture portable corpus had already passed with isolated workers before the final mechanical validator cleanup, and the post-cleanup lifecycle suite—including late-body-mutation rejection—passes. README Goals and North Star bars remain unchanged.

title: Decide reflaxe.ocaml native authority and target-lowering IR architecture
description: Define how Haxe-authored OCaml applications, compilers, and plugins obtain the practical capability of direct OCaml while preserving Haxe semantics, efficient generated code, and narrow runtime use. Decide the typed native escape-hatch ladder, Haxe and OCaml stdlib boundaries, external-library integration, export surface, and whether the current target AST needs narrow semantic plans or a broader validated target IR.
design: Accepted architecture: host-typed Haxe remains semantic authority; thin upstream-Haxe and hxhx adapters normalize immutable typed input and stable identities; one small typed OCaml-specific lowered model owns representation, places and evaluation schedules, calls/conversions, control effects, semantic runtime requirements, native dependencies, and export boundaries; OcamlExpr remains target syntax and OcamlASTPrinter remains semantic-free. Direction B is the incremental hard-cutover method and Direction C-lite is the durable target boundary. Reject a TypedExpr mirror, broad C-style CFG, shared cross-target representation IR, semantic annotations on OcamlExpr, permanent disconnected side tables, and a new lowering mega-file. The first admitted family is place/evaluation/assignment under haxe_ocaml-9v1va. Occurrence schedules must reproduce measured upstream Haxe behavior rather than memoize universally, and overloaded prefix/postfix result or mutation comes from the exact selected helper rather than fixity. Runtime selection moves to semantic reasons with the AST scan retained as a consistency check. Native capability uses direct lowering, typed ocaml facades, Haxe-friendly wrappers, generated first-order bindings, typed ml/mli adapters, then explicit raw authority. Unsupported states fail before OCaml output. One target core eventually serves both hosts without putting OCaml decisions into GenIrProgram or the plugin wire envelope.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Inventory current semantic, representation, runtime, native interop, raw authority, AST, printer, and build seams. 2) Define a typed escape-hatch ladder from direct lowering through native facades and handwritten OCaml adapters, with raw injection last and controlled. 3) Separate Haxe stdlib semantics, ocaml.* native APIs, external OCaml bindings, internal compatibility runtime, and exported OCaml-facing libraries. 4) Decide whether to retain OcamlExpr plus narrow validated plans or introduce a broader target-specific IR, with explicit evidence thresholds and rejected alternatives. 5) Define runtime selection, representation, source mapping, diagnostics, generated-code quality, plugin ABI, and performance invariants. 6) Compare committed reference implementations without importing their product-specific assumptions. 7) Prepare and validate a deep Oracle package with a controlling prompt and exact source/digest manifest. 8) Integrate the review against the live tree and complete a thinking:xhigh second pass before closing. 9) Do not claim current direct-OCaml capability or implement the architecture in the review slice.
notes:
GPT-5.6 PRO XHIGH SECOND-PASS ACCEPTANCE — 2026-07-18

Review provenance passed: candidate 83fda5964773c03804088fb2e2ec1dcbc2de8d31, archive SHA-256 561f9b40da8d7e473c4a4a2898ac5d14d2eba3978d68b1db143e378cd86e4b7b, 29 packaged payloads, and eight committed reference identities were independently verified. Live-tree spot checks confirmed the material diagnosis: carrier and layout ownership is split across OcamlCompiler and OcamlBuilder; raw interpolation stringifies child expressions early; stdlib guardrails can suppress errors while placeholder expressions survive; runtime requests outside the available set are silently filtered; ocamlc -i is only an inferred-interface aid; GenIrProgram is an explicit alias; and the current Stage3 emitter remains an independent semantic lowerer.

The response is accepted with two corrections from existing repo oracle evidence. First, place lowering records an occurrence schedule capable of sharing or repeating receiver/index/getter/setter evaluation; blanket exactly-once memoization is forbidden because overloaded indexed operations can evaluate read and write indexes separately. Second, ordinary numeric prefix/postfix semantics may record old/new results, but an overloaded abstract helper owns its own mutation and result; fixity never implies assign-back, reference ABI, or old/new return.

The accepted checkpoint is docs/00-project/ORACLE_CHECKPOINT_REFLAXE_OCAML_NATIVE_POWER_IR_2026_07_18.md. It records the practical direct-OCaml capability contract, C-lite model, ownership table, escape-hatch ladder, representation and runtime rules, typed import/adapter/export design, cross-host convergence, developer workflow, validation, stop conditions, human product defaults, release scope, and migration owners.

Follow-up graph: haxe_ocaml-9v1va first place/evaluation slice; haxe_ocaml-9bome representation/storage/capture; haxe_ocaml-taef5 calls/conversions; haxe_ocaml-w32h3 control effects; haxe_ocaml-0uwin semantic fail-closed runtime; haxe_ocaml-v8a9b typed imports/adapters/dependencies; haxe_ocaml-7sgtj curated exports; haxe_ocaml-1hd2w authoring/inspection workflow; existing M22 haxe_ocaml-bomhr and haxe_ocaml-fa0zh one-target-core integration. haxe_ocaml-s7jry now depends only on the concrete first semantic slice and fail-closed runtime work; later interop/convergence blocks only claims that include it.

THINKING:XHIGH SECOND-PASS REVIEW — 2026-07-18

1. Current verdict and authority: PASS. The decision keeps the monorepo today and does not authorize a physical move. A future move requires all E1-E8 evidence plus a measured product or maintenance trigger; no calendar date, version, or hxhx Full1 milestone silently causes extraction.
2. Standalone product truth: PASS. Stock Haxe package, runtime, examples, supported-host, and upstream-oracle evidence remain the primary reflaxe.ocaml product gates. hxhx is explicitly a major downstream workload, not the semantics authority or the only release proof.
3. Circular-gate risk: PASS. Q0/Q1 are owned by reflaxe.ocaml. Q2 is a bounded exact-artifact canary for shared contracts and release candidates. Q3 is scheduled, high-risk, and release-candidate E2E. Q4 remains hxhx release evidence. The plan does not serialize every target change behind Full1.
4. Dependency direction: PASS. reflaxe.ocaml remains independently usable with stock Haxe and cannot import hxhx compiler-core ownership. hxhx may consume a pinned target/runtime artifact. Local sibling overrides are allowed for speed but excluded from release evidence.
5. Semantic and ABI ownership: PASS. The split cannot create a second target core, runtime ABI, or schema owner. M22 retains authority to choose the home of its shared ABI; this decision only requires one versioned source of truth and packaged/generated consumers.
6. Coordinated changes and hard cutover: PASS. Immutable candidates and exact consumer pins permit paired validation without a permanent compatibility layer. The accepted consumer hard-cuts its pin; rollback selects the last green immutable artifact. Submodules, subtrees, moving branches, source mirrors, and rewritten releases are rejected.
7. Developer experience: PASS. The gate requires independent focused loops, explicit cache identity, cleanup, generated-OCaml inspection, and before/after timings. It rejects a split that materially slows common work without an accepted ownership or release benefit.
8. Provenance and migration: PASS. History filtering, MIT provenance, secret/path scanning, issue/docs ownership, release tags, and rollback are preconditions. This planning slice performs no history rewrite, publication, or repository creation.
9. Follow-up scope: PASS. haxe_ocaml-ko5le is preparation and clean-repository rehearsal only, waits for the standalone product owner, and cannot perform the authoritative move. A separate go decision and explicit execution scope are required.
10. Claims and priority: PASS. The decision changes architecture planning only. README Goals bars and current production-readiness claims remain unchanged. Existing Full1, standalone product, M22, and latency owners keep their scopes.

Review result: ACCEPT the repository extraction gate and close the decision bead. Continue to keep the monorepo until the rehearsal and trigger evidence support a later go decision.

title: Shorten the 45-minute Core Tests critical path without weakening it
description: The required Core PR workflow explicitly budgets about 45 minutes for one monolithic npm test job after four prerequisite jobs finish. That makes every pushed engineering checkpoint wait on a long serialized critical path even when the affected seams have already passed focused checks. Measure the suite internally, identify independent groups and shared setup costs, then reduce remote wall time without deleting tests, changing compiler semantics, weakening Stage0 restrictions, hiding failures, or making local validation less clear.
design: First capture per-phase wall time, setup time, rebuild/cache behavior, artifact mutation, and dependencies on an exact pushed commit. Preserve npm test as the complete local aggregate. In CI, shard only groups proven independent in separate clean runners or share an exact-SHA compiler artifact with verified provenance where that is cheaper. Keep one stable required Tests aggregate result for branch protection and evidence ownership. Fail closed if any shard is skipped, cancelled, stale, or missing. Compare critical-path time and total runner minutes so reduced latency is not purchased with unreasonable compute duplication.
acceptance_criteria: 1) An exact-run phase inventory identifies the dominant npm test costs and unsafe serialization boundaries. 2) Every command formerly run by the Core Tests job remains machine-inventoried and required. 3) Independent groups run concurrently without shared mutable artifacts or hidden ordering assumptions; intentionally serialized groups document why. 4) Any shared compiler artifact is bound to the exact commit, toolchain, build profile, and Stage0 policy and is verified before use. 5) A stable required Tests aggregate fails for failed, cancelled, skipped, or missing shards and remains compatible with branch-protection/evidence tooling. 6) Focused workflow-contract fixtures and an exact pushed Core run prove equal coverage with materially lower critical-path wall time; total runner-minute change is reported. 7) Local npm test remains a canonical complete command. 8) README Goals and North Star bars remain unchanged unless measured user-facing iteration readiness materially changes.
close_reason: The exact 106-command inventory, four clean-runner shards, fail-closed stable Tests aggregate, focused contract, and exact pushed Core run all passed; required wait time fell 48.3% without weakening coverage or Stage0 policy.

title: Block heavy local compiler runs under real memory pressure
description: The contention preflight records totalMemoryBytes and freeMemoryBytes but currently blocks only on normalized CPU load. During the server-leak tooling proof on 2026-07-18, the host fell to roughly 101 MiB reported free memory while many compiler processes were active. Load also blocked that run, but a low-load host with equivalent memory pressure would still be admitted and could spend minutes swapping, trigger an OOM, or corrupt timing evidence. Add an evidence-backed memory-capacity decision without conflating raw free pages with genuinely available memory.
design: Use a platform-aware available-memory signal and record how it was obtained. On systems that expose a stronger available/pressure metric, prefer it over Node os.freemem; treat collection failure explicitly. Define both an absolute reserve and a fraction-of-total threshold from measured hxhx/Reflaxe peak behavior, with deterministic fixture overrides. Preserve the existing auto policy: local heavy runs block with EX_TEMPFAIL, CI reports/warns because runner scheduling is external, and an explicit off override remains visible. Do not kill processes, reinterpret compiler correctness, or claim timing evidence from a pressured run.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Reports distinguish raw free memory from the selected platform-aware available-memory or pressure signal and name its provenance. 2) Evidence from representative hxhx/Reflaxe builds justifies reviewed absolute and proportional local thresholds. 3) A local heavy run returns the existing retryable exit before setup when memory alone is unsafe, while safe memory and CPU states pass. 4) CI auto policy warns instead of changing hosted-runner scheduling; off remains an explicit recorded override. 5) Deterministic fixtures cover memory-only block, CPU-only block, both, safe state, missing/invalid platform data, CI, and override behavior. 6) Beginner docs explain remediation without suggesting unrelated process termination. 7) Focused capacity, profiling, dev-loop, shell/JSON, and broad guards pass; README Goals and North Star bars remain unchanged.
notes: Implemented the reviewed available-memory policy. macOS uses memory_pressure -Q, Linux uses /proc/meminfo MemAvailable, Windows uses available physical memory, and unreviewed fallback data is reported as unavailable rather than treated like trustworthy capacity. The local reserve is max(4 GiB, 10% total): measured native compiler peaks are about 1.6-3.5 GiB, while the historical 7.2 GiB wrapper peak remains documented context. A live 32 GiB macOS sample showed 42%/roughly 12-14 GiB available while Node raw free memory was roughly 100 MiB, proving the false-block avoidance. JSON hard-cuts to hxhx.local-capacity-preflight.v2. Deterministic fixtures cover parsers, thresholds, safe, memory-only, CPU-only, both, raw-free discrepancy, unavailable/invalid, CI warn, off, shell/JSON, and stage0 pre-setup refusal. Focused capacity/profile/Gate3/latency/docs/path/mega-file/diff guards pass. README Goals and North Star bars remain unchanged because this improves developer workflow safety, not product readiness.
close_reason: Platform-aware memory admission, evidence-backed reserves, deterministic failure behavior, docs, and focused integration gates are complete.

comments.author: Marcelo Serpa
comments.text: Design evidence 2026-07-18 on the overloaded macOS host: Node reported totalMemoryBytes=34359738368 and raw freeMemoryBytes=128434176 (about 122 MiB), while /usr/bin/memory_pressure -Q reported 31% system-wide memory free (about 10.6 GiB of its available-memory model). vm_stat simultaneously showed only 3,606 raw free pages but 320,756 inactive pages and 958,638 compressor pages. This proves os.freemem alone would create a false memory block on macOS. The implementation should prefer the operating system available-memory/pressure signal, retain raw free memory as diagnostics only, and fixture the selected provenance. Threshold evidence still needs representative compiler peak measurements before code is changed.

comments.author: Marcelo Serpa
comments.text: Existing peak-memory evidence to use before choosing thresholds: the March 2026 bounded local Stage0 matrix measured native-auto at 2,320 MB and native fixed-job variants up to 3,534 MB, while the wrapper path reached 7,262 MB; the July clean stage0-free native A/B measured about 1.9 GiB child peak RSS; recent full/no-prepass Stage0 heartbeat traces reached roughly 1.6-2.4 GiB. Hosted Ubuntu Stage0-source evidence is much larger (about 15 GiB), but auto policy intentionally warns rather than schedules CI. This supports protecting several GiB of genuinely available local memory and retaining an override, but the exact absolute/fraction thresholds still require a reviewed workload/supported-host decision rather than copying the raw maximum.

title: Upgrade GitHub Actions off the deprecated Node 20 runtime

These action majors appear throughout the workflow fleet. Audit the current official successors and migrate the shared workflow surface before GitHub removes the compatibility bridge, preserving every existing cache, checkout-depth, artifact-retention, and evidence contract.
design: Treat this as one mechanical but broad CI-runtime migration. Use current official action release notes as the source of truth, inventory every workflow reference, update contract guards that intentionally assert action versions, and add a repository guard or single-source mechanism that prevents old Node-20 action majors from returning. Do not change the project Node toolchain merely because the JavaScript action host runtime changes. Keep behavior/evidence semantics unchanged and split any action-specific incompatibility into a focused follow-up rather than weakening gates.

comments.author: Marcelo Serpa
comments.text: Architecture comparison recorded 2026-07-18: haxe.c justifies its broad HxcIR because strict C does not preserve several interacting Haxe guarantees on its own: evaluation order, value-versus-place behavior, defined numeric conversions, ownership and lifetime, cleanup and failure edges, layout, and dispatch. Those decisions must be explicit before C emission, and scattered side tables would be a second hidden semantic model. HxcIR is therefore whole-program-shaped but target-owned and incrementally admitted; it is not evidence for a universal Reflaxe IR. OCaml already supplies managed memory, exceptions, algebraic values, references, and expression-oriented control flow, so its present semantic gap is smaller, though evaluation order and mutation still need explicit plans. Start with narrow validated target-local plans; consider a broader OCaml IR only if several extracted plans converge on shared nodes, identities, invariants, and validation needs. This is an evidence threshold, not a permanent prohibition.

title: Migrate the repository tracker from Beads 1.0.4 to 1.1.x safely
description: Beads 1.1.0 is the current stable release and includes migration, compaction, read-only, and recovery fixes. title: Keep profiler artifact paths stable across nested builds
description: The stage0 profiling wrapper accepts a relative output directory, but the inner build changes working directories. During the C++ prelude A/B, the compiler completed successfully while the requested per-class progress log was written somewhere the caller could not find. That makes a valid run look incomplete and wastes another multi-minute measurement.
design: Normalize the caller-provided output directory to an absolute path before any nested command can change directories. When per-class telemetry is requested, validate the expected log and summary before reporting success. Keep shell focused on orchestration and add deterministic fixture coverage for relative and absolute paths.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Relative and absolute output directories retain artifacts in the documented caller-visible location. 2) A successful profiling command fails clearly if requested telemetry is absent. 3) Fixture tests cover nested working-directory changes without running a real compiler. 4) Existing absolute-path profiling and benchmark-report validation remain green. 5) README Goals and North Star bars remain unchanged unless this changes production readiness.
close_reason: Relative and absolute profiler output paths now survive nested directory changes, incomplete successful telemetry fails deterministically, fixture coverage is wired into full guards, and the user/developer contract is documented.
