title: M22.4 — Implement hxhx host services v1 and capability negotiation
description:
Implement the first typed hxhx host catalog and low-risk post-backend service set using immutable snapshots and coarse calls. Provide deterministic negotiation for builtin and native-plugin backends, and honest unavailable or fallback adapters for host-neutral execution where correctness permits. Compiler facts remain data in the program/facts envelope; services are host-owned actions and do not smuggle mutable compiler state into target code.

Initial service candidates, subject to the M22.1 contract, include structured diagnostics, timers and telemetry, artifact/build-plan registration, resource or source lookup, incremental target cache operations, and selected immutable compiler facts delivered separately from actions.
acceptance_criteria:
1. hxhx publishes a typed, versioned catalog and immutable negotiation snapshot.
2. Builtin and plugin activation paths receive equivalent declared capabilities.
3. Evaluated and native host-neutral adapters expose only capabilities that genuinely exist and never pretend privileged services are present.
4. Required-semantic, optional-optimization, and optional-tooling behavior is deterministic.
5. Service use is batch-oriented and bridge overhead is measured.
6. Service implementations and target cores do not read hidden globals or ambient registration state.
7. Focused tests cover builtin, plugin, unavailable, valid fallback, version mismatch, and repeated compiler-server use.
8. No service can alter pre-backend compiler phases through this API.

Keep native execution, privileged-service access, and activation form visible as separate evidence dimensions.

2. A pinned real Reflaxe compiler family compiles a nontrivial application and runs its output.
3. External copyleft source remains fetched and pinned and is not vendored.
4. Evaluated versus native host-neutral baseline artifacts are byte-identical or normalized-equivalent with a documented reason.
5. Plugin versus builtin integrated artifacts and runtime behavior agree.
6. Required-service and optional-fallback cases are both exercised without conflating native execution with service availability.
7. Every proof records exact commit, host, execution and activation form, service catalog, ABI versions, plugin digest, generated artifact digest, runtime result, and stage0 policy.
8. Toy-only success cannot close the bead.

RETAINED QA CADENCE — 2026-07-19

This Bead is not a one-time demonstration. Its closure must leave a retained authentic compiler-promotion workload: one pinned nontrivial Haxe-authored Reflaxe compiler core exercised through evaluated host-neutral, stock-Haxe plugin, hxhx plugin, and hxhx builtin forms, with identical semantic core and verified payload/artifact identities. Neither should run for unrelated docs or application changes, and neither makes hxhx the sole reflaxe.ocaml correctness authority. title: M22.2 — Design and version the backend request and host-service ABI
description: Introduce the hard-cut versioned contract that carries the backend-facing program and facts, deterministic invocation configuration, declared execution form, and negotiated host capabilities. Replace string-only host-capability intent with typed and versioned requirements checked against what the host actually publishes. Keep execution form, host-service access, activation form, and the existing reflaxe.ocaml portable/metal code-generation profile as independent dimensions. Decide the bounded migration from the current `(program, BackendContext)` ABI without leaving a permanent dual interface.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A request/envelope design keeps `BackendContext` deterministic and configuration-only.
2. Typed service IDs, versions, requirement classes, and a host catalog are defined.
3. Execution form and privileged-service access are modeled independently; native execution does not imply integrated access.
4. Missing required semantic capabilities fail before backend creation or emission.
5. Manifest and builtin descriptors are checked against actual host availability, not merely non-empty strings.
6. Migration from the current v1 interface is a hard cutover with deterministic migration diagnostics and no backward-compatibility layer.
7. Dynlink representation uses versioned snapshots plus an opaque host handle by default; any direct generated-object crossing requires explicit identity evidence.
8. No general `Dynamic` service bag, mutable compiler context, or parser/typer implementation object crosses the boundary.
9. Focused fixtures cover unknown service, version mismatch, missing semantic requirement, optional fallback, duplicate declaration, and malformed manifest.
10. Any temporary bridge is added to the bridge inventory with an owner and an executable exit test.

title: M22.3 — Create the minimum versioned backend program and facts envelope
description: Strengthen the backend-facing program boundary only as far as the accepted M22 contract and real consumers require. Preserve the rule against a speculative compiler-wide neutral IR. Add explicit phase and version identity plus stable immutable facts and IDs needed by the selected pilots, while keeping target-specific semantics in target cores. M22 begins after the compiler has frozen the backend-facing program; it does not acquire authority over parsing, typing, macros, reachability, or other pre-backend phases.
acceptance_criteria:
1. The current `GenIrProgram` alias limitation is documented and the minimum envelope or an accepted bounded alternative is implemented.
2. Backend input states its phase invariants, version identity, and ownership after the macro lifecycle and backend-program freeze.
3. Facts are immutable, batched, and keyed by stable IDs wherever host object identity would otherwise leak.
4. At least two real consumers prove each shared fact is genuinely shared; one speculative target is insufficient.
5. The provisional reachability/retention snapshot is added only if the evidence and consumers justify it.
6. No target runtime semantics move into the common envelope and no compiler-wide universal IR rewrite begins.
7. Deterministic snapshot, equality, and serialization tests exist where practical.
8. Parser, resolver, typer, macro, and mutable compiler implementation objects are not exposed as plugin ABI.
notes:
GitHub issue #3 integration (2026-07-18): haxe_ocaml-9v1va owns target-local reflaxe.ocaml semantic-plan inventory and one evidence-backed OcamlBuilder extraction. M22.3 remains the cross-host versioned backend program/facts envelope; it must not absorb OcamlExpr, OCaml runtime intent, or target-local lowering plans. The two beads relate only where a genuinely shared, versioned semantic fact crosses the host/plugin boundary. GenIrProgram remains an alias under the existing two-consumer proof rule.
Accepted OCaml-lowering checkpoint 2026-07-18: the standalone target now deliberately owns a small typed OCaml-specific lowered model. That model, OcamlExpr, carrier choices, places, call plans, runtime requirements, dependency manifests, and export ABI remain outside the M22 host-neutral program/facts envelope. M22.3 supplies immutable typed bodies, resolved relationships, stable IDs, source spans, metadata, revision, and only genuinely shared batched facts. The two host adapters must support deterministic identity mapping without moving OCaml representation into GenIrProgram. Direction C-lite for the target does not change the no-universal-IR rule for M22.

title: M22.7 — Ship manifest and service negotiation v2 with native artifact compatibility
description: Extend plugin packaging so native artifacts declare execution presets, target-core identity, capability requirements, service API version, host and toolchain compatibility, and provenance. Validate the artifact before dynlink and define source-distributed rebuild and cache behavior. Follow the repository hard-cut compatibility policy: manifest v2 replaces v1 for this ABI rather than adding an indefinite compatibility layer.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A versioned manifest/schema includes backend ABI, backend program version, macro API version, host-service API version, typed requirements, supported presets, target-core ID/version, and artifact provenance.
2. Loader preflight rejects mismatches before `Dynlink.loadfile` wherever the manifest makes that possible.
3. The v1-to-v2 hard cutover is explicit and tested with deterministic migration diagnostics; no silent partial or backward compatibility remains.
4. Source/native rebuild cache keys include host version or commit, OS/architecture, OCaml version, ABI versions, execution and service preset, target-core version, and source digest.
5. Native plugin trust and process access are documented.
6. One target can be packaged as plugin and builtin without changing target semantics.
7. Negative fixtures cover host fingerprint, service version, service class, preset, artifact digest, and target-core mismatch.

title: M22.5 — Add host-neutral and hxhx-integrated Reflaxe adapters and execution presets
description: Evolve the current `ReflaxeTargetAdapter` direction into explicit adapters and named presets around one ordinary-Haxe, host-neutral target core. Evaluated host-neutral mode runs through upstream Haxe and public Reflaxe data. Native host-neutral mode compiles the same core with `reflaxe.ocaml` while masking privileged services. hxhx-integrated plugin and builtin modes negotiate the same service contract. These presets compose independent execution, service-access, activation, and OCaml code-generation dimensions rather than defining one overloaded profile axis.
acceptance_criteria:
1. One shared target core has no macro context, hxhx registration state, OCaml dynlink state, or ad-hoc environment reads.
2. `#if reflaxe_ocaml` and host-specific externs occur only in adapter, transport, optimized implementation, or composition-root modules.
3. A guard detects forbidden host imports and conditionals in the pilot target core.
4. Evaluated and native host-neutral presets emit equivalent artifacts for the baseline fixture.
5. hxhx plugin and builtin presets use the same target-core factory and semantics.
6. Capability declarations are independent from eval/native execution and plugin/builtin activation.
7. An explicitly named feature profile may select a larger integrated surface without scattering semantic conditionals.
8. Existing Reflaxe `BaseCompiler` targets get a documented migration adapter with bounded ownership and retirement criteria; emulation is not the final architecture.
9. hxhx parser, resolver, typer, macro lifecycle, and baseline diagnostics do not depend on Reflaxe framework APIs.

title: M22.6 — Prove one privileged semantic fact closes a real Reflaxe gap
description: Pressure-test the first privileged semantic fact against a real promoted target blocker. The provisional candidate is a read-only, batched reachability and retention snapshot motivated by real `reflaxe.elixir` keep/DCE pressure. Prove that portable public data is insufficient before standardizing it. M22 may report final host reachability facts to a backend, but it cannot change host reachability or introduce an earlier phase hook; if correctness needs pre-backend influence, hand that requirement to Stage4 or the general customization owner instead. Reject or replace the candidate if evidence does not support the contract.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Reproducible evidence explains why the portable public path is insufficient or ambiguous for a real target decision.
2. The host exposes a typed immutable semantic snapshot, not raw compiler records or an action service.
3. The integrated target consumes the fact in a real analysis or lowering decision.
4. Portable behavior is either proven correct through an explicit keep/root fallback or fails before emission with a clear requirement; it never silently approximates correctness-critical data.
5. Missing, stale, or mismatched fact data cannot silently change generated semantics.
6. Plugin and builtin behavior agree for the declared integrated scope.
7. Upstream Haxe 4.3.7 remains the behavior oracle; no upstream compiler implementation is copied or translated.
8. If pre-backend authority is required, the bead records the ownership handoff rather than expanding the M22 boundary.
9. A written xhigh second-pass review records whether the candidate was accepted, replaced, or rejected before any stable claim.

title: M22.11 — Productize SDK scaffolding, migration, docs, and support matrix
description: Make the proven SDK usable by target authors. Update scaffolding to generate one host-neutral core plus upstream-Haxe and hxhx adapters, explain independent execution/service/activation selection and conditionals at composition roots, document migration from existing Reflaxe compilers, and publish compatibility and troubleshooting guidance. Documentation must describe only commands and support levels backed by the preceding implementation evidence.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Scaffold layout keeps `core/` separate from `host/`, transport, and plugin glue.
2. Generated target core contains no host imports, macro context, or registration state.
3. Evaluated host-neutral, native host-neutral, plugin, and builtin commands are documented and smoke-tested.
4. Migration guidance covers current `BaseCompiler` and `DirectToStringCompiler` targets and identifies refactoring needed for advanced services.
5. Supported and unsupported services, execution forms, activation forms, hosts, OS/architecture, Haxe/OCaml versions, and artifact rebuild behavior are explicit.
6. Diagnostics distinguish not compiled natively, host lacks service, service version mismatch, and intentionally host-neutral execution.
7. Trust/security and pinned-upstream-adapter limits are plain language.
8. README and North Star wording changes only to match actual evidence; docs or scaffolding alone cannot move a progress bar.
notes: Native-power checkpoint integration 2026-07-18: haxe_ocaml-1hd2w owns the broader standalone reflaxe.ocaml authoring command group. M22.11 reuses it for plugin/target scaffolding and adds host adapters, ABI/payload packaging, migration, and support-matrix guidance. Required workflows include focused watch/build/test, lowered and representation inspection, runtime/dependency/raw/unsafe/export reports, binding and adapter checks, doctor, cross-host comparison, clean packaging, and phased performance. The ordinary loop must not rebuild all hxhx, regenerate bootstrap snapshots, or run every backend.

title: M22.1 — Freeze the Native Reflaxe Compiler SDK contract and ownership boundaries
description: Define the supported execution, service-access, and activation dimensions; backend request boundary; service taxonomy; phase ownership; conditional-compilation rules; ABI/versioning policy; security/trust model; and exact boundary with general hxhx customization. Inventory the current backend/plugin code and select the smallest first privileged semantic fact from real Reflaxe target pressure. This bead produces an accepted architecture contract, not implementation or a support claim.
acceptance_criteria: 1) docs/00-project/REFLAXE_NATIVE_COMPILER_SDK_M22_PLAN.md is complete and marked planning/contract status accurately. 2) Evaluated versus native execution, host-neutral versus hxhx-integrated service access, upstream/plugin/builtin activation, existing ocaml_profile=portable|metal, and unsafe-internal research are separated. 3) Immutable facts, host actions, pre-backend phase providers, and unsafe internals are distinct. 4) The contract decides the default OCaml dynlink representation and proof required before direct typed-object passing. 5) The first privileged semantic candidate is selected from real evidence with fallback/fail-fast behavior and no authority to change frontend reachability. 6) Ownership with haxe_ocaml-h5jta, haxe_ocaml-38gsp, Stage3, Stage4, and upstream-Haxe adapters is unambiguous. 7) No public readiness bar changes. 8) Written xhigh second-pass review is recorded.
notes: Architecture review uses the revised dimensional model: execution form, service access, activation/packaging, and ocaml_profile are independent. M22 v1 begins only after the backend-facing program is frozen. Default dynlink transport is a canonical versioned snapshot plus opaque handle; direct generated-object passing requires separate proof. The first semantic candidate is a read-only final reachability/retention snapshot, with public keep/root declarations as the host-neutral fallback and no M22 authority to change DCE.
close_reason: Accepted planning contract: canonical M22 plan completed, independent dimensions and post-backend ownership fixed, provisional reachability snapshot bounded, actual child graph recorded, no cycles found, and written xhigh second-pass review passed. No implementation, ABI/version, readiness, or release-evidence change.

comments.author: Marcelo Serpa
comments.text:
XHIGH SECOND-PASS REVIEW — 2026-07-15

1. Owner overlap and cycles: PASS. haxe_ocaml-38gsp owns the release-grade stage0-free combined product; haxe_ocaml-h5jta owns general compiler customization and variation; M22 owns backend/target authoring services only after the backend-facing program is frozen. bd dep cycles reports no dependency cycle.
2. Full1 priority: PASS. M22 is milestone:M22 and phase:post-1.0. The existing Full1 block is preserved, M22.2 and M22.3 have explicit Full1 blockers, and M22.1 was contract-only work. No M17/Full1 evidence or readiness criterion was weakened.
3. Raw compiler context: PASS. The contract permits typed immutable facts, coarse capability-limited actions, and opaque handles. It forbids a Dynamic service bag, mutable compiler records, hidden globals, and parser/typer objects in the plugin ABI.

title: Let JS resolve generic constructor names in Gate3

title: Find why a clean bootstrap benchmark rewrites committed snapshots
description: A successful warm bootstrap benchmark began from a clean checkout but ended with tracked source changes. In plain language: running the official generator produced generated OCaml files that differ from the versions already committed. This does not invalidate the timing samples, because the unmeasured prime happened before every measured run, but it is a correctness and maintenance question that needs its own owner. Identify exactly which generated files change and why. Do not edit generated .ml files by hand; any fix must happen in the Haxe source or official regeneration tooling.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Reproduce from a clean checkout at a recorded commit, or enhance the benchmark artifact so it records every changed tracked path. 2) Record the exact changed paths and before/after digests. 3) Classify the cause as stale committed snapshots, nondeterministic generation, policy-dependent generation, or another clearly explained source. 4) If a correction is needed, change only repo-owned Haxe source or official generation scripts, then regenerate through the supported command; never hand-edit generated ML. 5) Run the focused bootstrap checks and repository guards, and record whether the committed snapshot becomes clean and repeatable. 6) Review README Goals status; do not change readiness bars unless user-facing production readiness actually changes.
close_reason: Classified clean bootstrap drift as deterministic stale generated output, stabilized Reflaxe metadata, added exact path/digest reporting, verified the refreshed output builds stage0-free, and filed haxe_ocaml-wycun for deliberate snapshot promotion.

title: Modular hxhx customization and Haxe-family variation architecture
description: Define and eventually implement the architecture for bending hxhx/Haxe without corrupting the baseline Haxe 4.3.7 compatibility contract. This owns two related goals from docs/00-project/NORTH_STAR_GOALS.md: pluggable compiler customization and deliberate Haxe-family compiler variations/forks in Haxe. The baseline hxhx release must remain Haxe-compatible by default; custom behavior must be explicit, removable, documented, and CI-auditable.
acceptance_criteria: 1) A design doc defines supported extension points for compiler customization versus full compiler variations/dialects. 2) The model keeps baseline hxhx Haxe 4.3.7 compatibility as the default and prevents plugins/variations from silently weakening parity claims. 3) At least one minimal pluggable customization proof exists with enable/disable behavior and deterministic tests. 4) At least one documented variation/fork workflow exists for creating a deliberate Haxe-family compiler product in Haxe. 5) README Goals status and docs/00-project/NORTH_STAR_GOALS.md are updated when production-readiness changes.
close_reason: Completed epic: Reflaxe/hxhx boundary accepted, customization/variation architecture documented, minimal Stage3 customization enable/disable proof implemented and tested, Haxe-family variation workflow documented, README Goals/North Star reviewed with progress bars unchanged, and child validation evidence recorded.

comments.author: Marcelo Serpa
comments.text: Scope clarification: this track is not only about plugins. A core reason for hxhx is to make Haxe itself easier to hack because the compiler is implemented in Haxe. Design work should therefore cover compiler readability, modular seams, behavior-driven tests for safe edits, and deliberate fork/variation workflows, while keeping baseline hxhx Haxe 4.3.7-compatible by default.

comments.author: Marcelo Serpa
comments.text: Second-pass design review for xhigh scope: the KPI patch removes eager startup registration of generated Type metadata and installs HxTypeRegistry.init as a lazy HxType hook before main. This preserves reflection semantics because Type.resolveClass/resolveEnum, Type.get*Fields, Type.createInstance/createEnum, enumConstructor, typed-catch tag lookup, and Std.isOfType now force the hook before reading registry tables. Registration helpers intentionally do not force initialization, because HxTypeRegistry.init is implemented in terms of those helpers; setting registry_initialized before invoking the hook avoids reentrant initialization. This is a performance-only implementation change, not a scope/policy exception. Local evidence before remote KPI rerun: stage0-free no-emit smoke passed stage3=no_emit_ok with resolved_modules=1; PORTABLE_FIXTURE_ALLOWLIST=type_reflection_basic,typed_catches,typed_catches_dynamic bash scripts/test-portable.sh passed; npm run test:snapshot passed; npm run ci:guards and git diff --check passed. It validates stage3=ok, generated OCaml source count, a built reported artifact, and clean bootstrap snapshot diff.

title: Stage0 memory: bootstrap payload strategy spike
description:
Current-head evidence rejects source-shape helper splitting, no-display trimming, no-internal-tools/no-stage3 standalone promotion, DCE, and runtime knobs as stable equivalent mitigations. The remaining credible path is a deliberate driver/payload strategy review and bounded prototype that reduces the pre-Reflaxe macro/eval typed-module payload wall without making non-equivalent release claims.

Acceptance:
1. Record a second-pass design review for the driver/payload seam, including rejected shortcuts and release-equivalence risks.
2. Identify one bounded prototype that can be validated with compile-only checks plus direct stage0 RSS evidence.
3. Implement the bounded prototype only if it preserves release-equivalence or is explicitly profiling-only; record accept/reject evidence and artifact sizes.
close_reason: Xhigh second-pass review complete; no safe quick payload shortcut selected. Filed dedicated stage0-free refresh architecture follow-up.

comments.author: Marcelo Serpa
comments.text:
Second-pass driver/payload strategy review (thinking:xhigh).

Evidence reviewed:
- Multi-sample native stacks show the retained wall inside stage0 macro/eval typed-module encoding: MacroContext/MacroApi/EvalEncode/EvalEmitter, with later GC pressure in encode_type.
- Reflaxe progress/onOutputComplete hooks still do not fire inside the first 120-300s windows, so the wall is before backend output progress.
- Callback-collapse already removed the extra onAfterTyping typed-module callback; the remaining full typed payload is Reflaxe's custom-target/DirectToStringCompiler pass itself.
- Source-shape/helper extraction families are rejected or low-single-digit only: parser, macro scanner/client, ExprMacroExpander, TyperStage.
- Flag/graph trims are rejected as release defaults: no-internal-tools, no-stage3, no-display, no-hx-parser, DCE. The no-stage3+no-internal-tools collapse is real but non-equivalent because it removes the native driver/internal surface from the generated compiler.

Rejected shortcuts:
- Promote no-stage3/no-internal-tools/no-display as committed snapshot defaults: non-equivalent or empirically regressive.
- Add another Context.onAfterTyping/onGenerate side channel: worsens the macro/eval typed payload that is already the sampled wall.
- Keep splitting large Haxe source files blindly: current-head evidence is 0-for-several on the remaining hotspots and often increases RSS.
- Treat ocaml_emit_only or --no-output as payload eliminators: they only skip build/backend output details after the typed graph has already crossed the macro/eval boundary.

Equivalence boundary:
- For release/runtime paths, stage0 source regeneration is already outside the normal path. build-hxhx.sh defaults to committed bootstrap snapshots and release/dist paths enforce HXHX_FORBID_STAGE0=1.
- Therefore the honest release mitigation is to keep normal builds/stage0-forbidden gates on snapshots and treat stage0 source regen as maintainer-only diagnostic work until native/self-hosted refresh exists.
- Full1 perf parity should measure hxhx runtime/native lanes vs upstream haxe, not a maintainer-only stage0 Reflaxe snapshot refresh wall.

Next credible architecture prototype:
- Stage0-free bootstrap refresh or payload slicing, not another Haxe flag:
  1. Native/self-hosted refresh: use built hxhx/Stage3 to regenerate packages/hxhx/bootstrap_out without upstream stage0 haxe.
  2. Monolithic payload slicing: split hxhx bootstrap generation into separately generated/linkable artifacts so no single stage0 Reflaxe invocation has to encode the full Main+Stage3+internal-tools typed graph.
- Both are release-scope architecture work and need their own xhigh design/implementation beads; they are not safe as a quick memory-tuning patch.

Bounded implementation decision for this bead:
- Do not implement a new payload shortcut in this slice. The safe bounded action is to update policy/evidence and move to a dedicated stage0-free refresh/payload-slicing task.
- Immediate local follow-up should also fix bootstrap temp retention, because repeated snapshot builds currently leave large ignored .tmp/hxhx-bootstrap-build.* directories and the user has hit disk pressure.

title: Stage0 memory: driver payload strategy review
description: Review implementation-grade options to reduce or avoid stage0's compiler-sized Reflaxe typed callback payload after stack sampling confirmed the wall is upstream Haxe macro/eval type encoding. This is xhigh because it affects release/perf evidence semantics and bootstrap driver scope.

close_reason: Second-pass review complete; selected bounded no-display profiling trim before broader driver split.

comments.author: Marcelo Serpa
comments.text:
Second-pass design review for post-stack-sample stage0 memory seam.

Context/evidence:
- `haxe.ocaml-a0pt.1.26` confirmed the current 120s wall is before Reflaxe progress hooks.
- 25s/55s samples are dominated by upstream macro/eval callback execution (`MacroContext`, `MacroApi`, `EvalEmitter`, `EvalEncode`).
- 85s shifts into `MacroApi.encode_type` / `EvalEncode` plus GC pressure.
- Prior A/B evidence rejects broad source-shape splits, `--ocaml-only`, standalone `--no-internal-tools`, standalone `--no-stage3`, `--dce full`, extra callback registration, and cheap graph trims as closure paths.

Rejected options:
- Promote `--no-internal-tools` or `--no-stage3` as default: rejected. The former is non-equivalent as a huge signal and standalone current-head runs regress; the latter standalone also regresses. These cannot support honest Full 1.0 evidence.
- Add or rely on another `Context.onAfterTyping`/macro callback: rejected. The stack evidence and callback-collapse fix show each extra typed callback payload is exactly the expensive surface.
- Try to make Reflaxe avoid typed-module payload entirely in stage0: reject for this slice. That changes target macro architecture and crosses release/provenance semantics; it needs a larger driver/payload design, not a drive-by mitigation.
- Keep doing broad helper/file splits in parser/macro/typer hotspots: rejected. Multiple current-head profiles have already shown regressions or non-durable wins, and the new stack evidence points above those repo-local helper boundaries.

Accepted bounded seam before broad driver split:
- Make the existing `HXHX_STAGE0_NO_DISPLAY` profiling knob real and measurable.
- Rationale:
  - `scripts/hxhx/build-hxhx.sh` already defines and forwards `-D hxhx_stage0_no_display`.
  - There is no matching source guard in `packages/hxhx/src`, and `scripts/hxhx/regenerate-hxhx-bootstrap.sh` / `profile-stage0-regen.sh` do not expose the knob.
  - `DisplayResponseSynthesizer.hx` is 742 lines and Stage3Compiler has display/server integration points. This is a plausible compile-graph trim that is narrower than disabling all Stage3 or all internal tools.
  - If implemented as profiling-only, it does not alter release snapshots or Full 1.0 claims; any evidence must be labelled non-default unless a later parity review promotes it.

Implementation guardrails for the accepted seam:
- Add source guards so `hxhx_stage0_no_display` compiles out display synthesis/request inference only in profiling lanes.
- Add regen/profile pass-through and report fields so A/B evidence is reproducible.
- Validate compile-only with and without `-D hxhx_stage0_no_display`; run guards.
- Profile as an A/B candidate and reject unless it is equivalent-fail-mode and materially improves peak RSS.

Decision:
- Close this xhigh review as a completed second-pass review.
- Open/execute a bounded `thinking:high` child for the no-display profiling trim.
- Do not start broad driver/payload implementation until this narrower existing-dead-knob seam is resolved.

title: Define native source-host adapter contract for Reflaxe-style custom-target HXML workflows
description: The pybm verifier now proves that ordinary source-based reflaxe.elixir HXML workflows (for example compile.hxml/build-tests.hxml using -D elixir_output plus CompilerInit.Start()) do not currently map onto any native hxhx host lane. This is broader than a simple CLI parse bug: Stage3 currently supports builtin JS/OCaml lanes and explicit backend provider/plugin activation, but no generic source-host adapter contract for Reflaxe-style custom targets. We need an explicit design decision for whether and how hxhx should support these workflows natively.
acceptance_criteria: 1. A written contract explains whether source-based Reflaxe target HXML workflows are in scope for native hxhx-as-haxe support, with concrete trigger signals and routing rules. 2. The chosen path is explicit: either (a) implement a minimal native host-adapter surface for one real workflow such as reflaxe.elixir compile.hxml, or (b) document that pybm must use a different native artifact/host path and update verifier/docs accordingly. 3. The outcome is recorded in bead comments/docs with artifact references from pybm, not left as an implicit assumption.
close_reason: Closed after explicit written second-pass design review. The repo contract now recommends explicit host-adapter/plugin lanes as the official native verification path for external Reflaxe workloads, keeps raw source-based HXML invocations as diagnostic baseline evidence, updates docs to match, and creates follow-up bead haxe.ocaml-k6rz to enforce that contract in the verifier.

comments.author: Marcelo Serpa
comments.text: Initial design note (2026-03-18): local evidence narrows this to three real paths, not one. (A) Add a native source-host adapter lane in hxhx itself: detect a source-based Reflaxe custom-target workflow (for example elixir_output + CompilerInit.Start or similar explicit markers) and route it into Stage3 with a declared backend/provider contract. This would make hxhx act as a true haxe replacement for these workflows, but it expands CLI/compiler scope and needs a crisp contract for how source libraries expose provider metadata. (B) Keep core hxhx strict and require explicit host adapters/plugin manifests for native use, then update pybm to verify the native artifact through that adapter path instead of raw haxe compile.hxml compatibility. This matches existing docs/02-user-guide/HXHX_PROMOTION_HOST_ADAPTERS.md and the proven promotion lanes. (C) Explicitly declare raw source-based Reflaxe-target HXML workflows out of scope for native host replacement and keep pybm as a diagnostic-only baseline comparison tool. Current repo state favors B or C more than A: Stage3 already supports builtin JS/OCaml plus explicit provider/plugin activation, but there is no generic source-host adapter surface and no native Elixir backend provider in vendor/reflaxe-elixir to auto-discover.

comments.author: Marcelo Serpa
comments.text:
Second-pass design review (written fallback for thinking:xhigh, 2026-03-18).

Decision question
- Should native `hxhx` invoked as a `haxe` replacement be required to accept ordinary source-based Reflaxe custom-target HXML workflows such as `vendor/reflaxe-elixir/test/snapshot/core/try_catch/compile.hxml` and `vendor/reflaxe-elixir/examples/todo-app/build-tests.hxml`, or should native support remain scoped to declared host-adapter/plugin lanes?

Evidence reviewed
- Artifact: `.artifacts/pybm/reflaxe-elixir-native-verify/20260318-174627/reflaxe-elixir-native-verify.summary.json`
  - upstream `runtime-smoke`: pass
  - native `runtime-smoke`: fail
  - `primaryNativeFailureCategory=native_source_target_unimplemented`
- Native route planner: `packages/hxhx/src/hxhx/CliRouting.hx`
  - native lanes are currently explicit: `--ocaml`, standard `--js`, `--ocaml-eval`, `--compat`
  - no generic route exists for source-based Reflaxe custom-target workflows
- Stage3 backend loading: `packages/hxhx/src/hxhx/Stage3Compiler.hx`
  - native dynamic backend support is explicit-provider / explicit-plugin-manifest based
  - no source-host discovery contract exists for `-D elixir_output=...` + `CompilerInit.Start()` style workflows
- Promotion doctrine: `docs/02-user-guide/HXHX_PROMOTION_HOST_ADAPTERS.md` and `docs/00-project/REFLAXE_PROMOTION_MATRIX_CONTRACT.md`
  - current native promotion contract is adapter/plugin based
  - supported official paths are builtin target and explicit plugin path, not implicit raw-source custom-target discovery
- Pressure-test workflow shape:
  - `vendor/reflaxe-elixir/test/snapshot/core/try_catch/compile.hxml` uses `-D elixir_output=out` plus `--macro reflaxe.elixir.CompilerInit.Start()`
  - `vendor/reflaxe-elixir/examples/todo-app/build-tests.hxml` uses `-D elixir_output=test/generated` and `-lib reflaxe.elixir`
  - neither declares an `hxhx_backend_plugin_manifest` or `hxhx_backend_provider`

Option review
- A) Add native source-host adapter discovery to `hxhx` itself
  - upside: strongest `hxhx as haxe replacement` story for Reflaxe custom targets
  - cost: new CLI/compiler contract, backend metadata discovery design, likely broader scope than current promotion matrix, and risk of inventing semantics that upstream Haxe does not define as a native `hxhx` concern
  - current repo evidence does not yet justify this as the default path
- B) Keep official native support on explicit host-adapter/plugin lanes and make `pybm` verify that declared path
  - upside: matches current promotion docs, current Stage3 ABI, and already-proven `RPMX_HXHX_PLUGIN:PASS` lane
  - keeps native support honest and measurable
  - lets raw source-based HXML workflows remain a diagnostic comparison instead of an implied support contract
- C) Explicitly declare raw source-based Reflaxe-target HXML workflows out of scope for native `hxhx-as-haxe`
  - upside: cleanest boundary
  - cost: too negative alone; it would leave `pybm` without an official native verification path unless paired with B

Recommendation
- Choose B as the official path, with C only as the diagnostic boundary statement for raw source-host invocations.
- Concretely: native support for external Reflaxe targets should be measured through declared promotion host adapters/plugins, not by assuming `hxhx` already auto-discovers arbitrary source-based custom-target HXML workflows.
- Raw source-based `reflaxe.elixir` invocations should remain useful baseline diagnostics, but they should not be treated as required native compatibility proofs unless we later explicitly widen scope and implement A.

Implications for existing beads
- `haxe.ocaml-pybm.1` should no longer be treated as an unconditional must-fix compatibility bug. Under the recommended contract, it is either:
  - superseded by adapter-path verification work, or
  - retained only as a diagnostic gap bead if we want to track a future scope expansion toward A.
- The next implementation bead should adapt the verifier/docs so the official native lane is the promoted adapter/plugin path and the raw source-based lane is labeled diagnostic/baseline.

Acceptance boundary for closing this bead
- This bead can close once the repo docs and pybm tracking explicitly adopt the recommendation above and the next implementation bead exists to enforce it in verifier output.

comments.text: 2026-04-15 design review for strict Gate3 echo harness: latest run 24445287437 proved the wrapper/watchdog fix. Macro passed in direct mode and summary validation failed immediately without the old one-hour timeout tail. Remaining blocker moved to the shared runci echo-server setup: every non-Macro target first runs haxe build.hxml in tests/echoServer, whose HXML selects -neko www/echoServer.n. Closing bxlg.9.5 before either (a) widening the runtime Type model enough to make those semantics honest, or (b) explicitly scoping them out of Full1, would be misleading. But it is still below an honest Full1 macro API parity claim. Two semantic seams remain material: (1) synthetic abstract-wrapper fidelity is still missing, so followWithAbstracts/applyTypeParameters over abstract-heavy paths still collapse to underlying types instead of preserving a real abstract wrapper; (2) synthetic module/type metadata is still narrower than upstream because enum/typedef/abstract declaration kinds still round-trip as class-shaped refs in external-host mode. title: M17 — Full1 candidate closure: declared Haxe 4.3.7 equivalence, performance, and prepublication go/no-go
description: Strict Full 1.0 closure track for hxhx itself. Prove the owner-approved Haxe 4.3.7 compatibility scope for one candidate SHA: current-head required lanes, strict upstream suites, declared targets/toolchains, macro/eval, plugin workload/parity, performance, and an authentic prepublication RC consumed by release. This epic does not own standalone reflaxe.ocaml product readiness, the combined hxhx plus reflaxe.ocaml route, or the broader promotion product.

title: Stage0 RSS source-level mitigation beyond runtime flags
description:
Repeated A/B probes with current runtime/build knobs do not yield stable >=20% median RSS reduction in failfast windows (90s/120s). We need source-level mitigation work targeting dominant compiler contributors rather than more flag sweeps.

- disable-prepasses (120s, reps=3): median reduction ~4.19%
- no-opt+disable-prepasses (120s, reps=3): median reduction ~3.10%
- disable-prepasses+s=2M (120s, reps=3): median regression ~-17.97%
- disable-prepasses (90s, reps=3): median reduction ~1.94%

Scope:
1) Identify a concrete source-level mitigation candidate (e.g., reducing retained AST/metadata in hot phases, staged emit partitioning, or pass-level memory reclamation points) with explicit rationale.
2) Implement the mitigation behind a deterministic toggle for A/B verification.
3) Validate with repeated A/B runner (reps>=3) and report median reduction on 120s failfast probes.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Mitigation implementation lands with docs on what it changes and why.\n2) Repeated A/B evidence (120s failfast, reps>=3) is attached as artifacts with summary.json.\n3) Either achieves >=20% median reduction OR documents why not and proposes next measurable mitigation with residual-risk note.

title: Stage0 --connect handoff hang after source emit (client waits while server idle)
description: During source builds with repo server reuse (HXHX_STAGE0_USE_REPO_SERVER=1), the stage0 run can finish generation and populate packages/hxhx/out/**, but the `haxe build.hxml -D ocaml_build=byte --connect <port>` client remains blocked indefinitely. In one run, both client and server dropped to near-idle while the build script kept waiting, requiring manual kill and a direct `dune build ./out.bc` continuation. This creates long false hangs and hides successful progress.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Repro command is deterministic and documented (build-hxhx source lane with --connect). 2) Build script detects stalled or idle --connect handoff and fails fast with actionable message OR auto-recovers by switching to direct non-connect stage0 invocation. 3) On success, script always exits with produced out.bc/out.exe path and no manual kill needed. 4) Add regression coverage (scripted smoke) and doc guidance for when to disable HXHX_STAGE0_USE_REPO_SERVER.
notes: Implemented connect-handoff auto-recovery in scripts/hxhx/build-hxhx.sh: if --connect lane is idle (no log growth + idle process tree) for HXHX_STAGE0_CONNECT_IDLE_SECS, kill stalled client and retry once without --connect. Added deterministic regression smoke scripts/hxhx/test-build-hxhx-connect-retry.sh (npm run test:hxhx:build-connect-retry-smoke), wired into .github/workflows/ci.yml guards job, and documented knob in README.md + docs/01-getting-started/TESTING.md. Local validation: npm run test:hxhx:build-connect-retry-smoke, npm run ci:guards, npm run test:hxhx:cli-contract.
close_reason: Implemented connect stall detector + auto-retry without --connect, added CI smoke coverage, and documented operator knobs.

title: Bootstrap/source build throughput: native stage0 default + configurable dune workers
description:
Context from 2026-03-04 sessions:
- Running stage0/source lane through the Lix shim (which haxe -> ~/.nvm/.../lix/bin/haxeshim.js) showed severe memory/time behavior (multiple GB spikes; long tail builds).
- Switching to native Haxe binary (/Users/fullofcaffeine/haxe/versions/4.3.7/haxe) immediately improved early heartbeat RSS (roughly from ~7GB windows to ~1.2GB windows in comparable probes) and smoother progress.
- Build path in focus: scripts/hxhx/build-hxhx.sh (source lane with HXHX_FORCE_STAGE0=1) and bootstrap compile via dune.

Problem statement:
Even with native stage0 selection policy work underway, developer UX is still poor for full source rebuilds and CI reruns. We need deterministic, documented throughput controls (especially worker parallelism) and benchmark evidence for safe defaults on local + CI environments.

Scope:
1) Add explicit, documented worker controls for relevant build steps:
   - stage0 Haxe source build lane (where applicable)
   - dune bootstrap build lane (out.bc/out.exe)
2) Benchmark matrix for representative settings:
   - native-vs-wrapper stage0 binary
   - worker counts (e.g., auto, 1, 2, 4, 8)
   - collect wall time + peak RSS from existing heartbeat/report telemetry
3) Choose safe default(s) and expose override knobs in scripts/docs.
4) Ensure CI reproducibility: same knobs available in workflow env with clear marker output.
acceptance_criteria:
1) build-hxhx lane supports deterministic worker configuration via env/flag (documented in scripts/hxhx/build-hxhx.sh help/docs).
2) A benchmark artifact/table is produced for at least one local run and one CI-like run, showing time + peak RSS across worker settings and stage0 binary modes.
3) Selected default setting is justified in docs (STAGE0_POLICY + TESTING + README quick note), including when to override.
4) CI logs include resolved stage0 binary path and effective worker configuration for auditable runs.
5) No behavioral regressions: npm run -s ci:guards passes and gate scripts still execute with default knobs.
close_reason: Implemented worker matrix controls, benchmark artifact table (local + CI-like), docs default/override guidance, and guard validation.

title: Bootstrap regen reliability: stage0 binary resolution (native vs wrapper)
description:
During `scripts/hxhx/regenerate-hxhx-bootstrap.sh`, default stage0 resolution (`HAXE_BIN=haxe`) picked `/Users/fullofcaffeine/.nvm/versions/node/v20.19.3/bin/haxe` (Node wrapper), not the native Haxe binary.

Observed in this session:
- Wrapper-backed runs showed prolonged emit stalls with heartbeats up to 700s+ and RSS spikes around 5-7GB.
- Rerun with `HAXE_BIN=/Users/fullofcaffeine/haxe/versions/4.3.7/haxe` showed immediate improvement (early heartbeat RSS ~1.2GB) and materially healthier behavior.

Question to resolve:
- Is wrapper selection expected for bootstrap regen lanes, or should we default to native stage0 Haxe for deterministic resource/latency behavior?

Scope:
1) Reproduce benchmarked comparison (wrapper vs native binary) with report artifacts.
2) Decide bootstrap-stage0 binary selection policy and make default explicit.
3) Implement guardrails (warning/fail-fast/doc guidance) when wrapper binary is detected in critical regen lanes.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Add a documented policy for stage0 binary selection in bootstrap regen (default + override behavior).
2) Add a deterministic check/report in regen flow that logs resolved stage0 binary path and identifies wrapper-vs-native mode.
3) Add regression/perf evidence (at least one reproducible measurement command) proving selected default avoids pathological memory/time behavior.
4) Update docs (`STAGE0_POLICY` and bootstrap/testing docs) with exact commands and troubleshooting guidance.
close_reason: Policy/reporting/benchmark acceptance complete; remaining RSS optimization tracked in child haxe.ocaml-a0pt.1.

comments.author: Marcelo Serpa

Repro command used:
- HXHX_BOOTSTRAP_HEARTBEAT=20 HXHX_BOOTSTRAP_BUILD_TIMEOUT_SECS=1800 bash scripts/hxhx/build-hxhx.sh

Observed behavior:

- Peak transient compiler process: ocamlc.opt -impl EmitterStage.ml with RSS around ~2.0GB (sampled via ps), then dropping as compile progressed.

Interpretation:
- There are likely two separate contributors to memory/runtime pain:
  1) stage0 Haxe wrapper-vs-native binary choice (existing issue scope), and
  2) OCaml bootstrap compile pressure from large generated units (not stage0).

Suggested expansion for this follow-up (or linked child task):
- Capture both dimensions in measurements: stage0 regen memory (wrapper vs native) and bootstrap compile memory (ocamlc.opt on EmitterStage.ml) so root causes are not conflated.

comments.author: Marcelo Serpa
comments.text:
RCA + fix summary:

- Root cause was runtime unsoundness in generated OCaml values used across the stage0-policy runtime check path:
  1) non-void nested-return fallback generation used defaultValueForType(...) in a way that could substitute sentinel defaults instead of preserving the computed body value, and
  2) string equality could still reach String.equal on non-string Obj payloads under poisoned/null-sentinel flows.
- Fixes applied:
  - packages/reflaxe.ocaml/src/reflaxe/ocaml/ast/OcamlBuilder.hx
    - defaultValueForType now uses Obj.magic HxRuntime.hx_null for anyNull (instead of Obj.magic ()).
    - nested-return fallback in both function builders now preserves the computed result and explicitly coerces via Obj.magic fallback_result rather than discarding to a type default.
  - packages/reflaxe.ocaml/std/runtime/HxString.ml
    - hardened equals with Obj-level guards:
      - exact hx_null pointer checks first
      - Obj.string_tag verification before String.equal
      - returns false for non-string payloads instead of invoking string equality on invalid values.
  - Regenerated bootstrap snapshot under packages/hxhx/bootstrap_out/* so stage0-forbidden runtime checks consume the fixed runtime/emission.

Validation on Darwin:
- npm run -s test:stage0-policy:release (pass)
- repeated stability loop: 3 consecutive passes of npm run -s test:stage0-policy:release
- targeted regressions:
  - npm run -s test:m14:hih-try-throw-stmt
  - npm run -s test:m14:hih-optional-int-null-padding-runtime
  - portable fixtures: typed_catches_dynamic, dynamic_equality, exceptions_basic
- npm run -s ci:guards (pass)

Result: no exit 139 observed across repeated release stage0-policy runs.

title: README rebrand to hxhx + upstream reflaxe.ocaml guide

Problem
- README is still titled `reflaxe.ocaml`, while the repo is now hxhx-first.
- We need clear top-level project goals and explicit positioning for hxhx + reflaxe.ocaml.
- We also need a dedicated beginner-friendly guide for using reflaxe.ocaml with upstream Haxe.

Goal
- Rebrand top-level docs around `hxhx` while keeping reflaxe.ocaml clearly documented and usable.

Scope
1) Update README title/intro/goals to hxhx-first framing.
2) Add explicit goals:
   - easier to understand compiler implementation
   - easier to modify compiler behavior
   - parity target with upstream Haxe 4.3.7
   - clean-room MIT positioning for embedded/commercial usage
   - native compilation path for Reflaxe compilers/targets for performance
   - keep reflaxe.ocaml usable with upstream Haxe while co-developing in this monorepo
3) Add dedicated upstream usage doc under docs/01-getting-started and link from README.
4) Align docs/00-project/BOUNDARIES.md wording with this positioning.

Acceptance criteria
- README title is `hxhx` with updated goals/positioning.
- New upstream guide exists and is linked from README.
- boundaries doc reflects hxhx-primary + reflaxe.ocaml dual role and monorepo rationale.
- ci:guards passes.

title: Gate1: module-local helper types (multi-class modules)
description:
Upstream Gate1 (tests/unit/compile-macro.hxml) includes many modules that declare helper types in the same .hx file (for example: private class CastHelper inside TestNumericCasts.hx). Today the Stage3 pipeline models only the module's main class, so OCaml emission fails with errors like: Unbound module CastHelper.

Implement enough of Haxe's multi-type module semantics for Gate1 bring-up:
- Discover additional class declarations in a module (at least names and static vars/constants).
- Preserve them on the Haxe side (HxModuleDecl must expose all classes in the module).
- Make Stage3 emission generate OCaml providers for those helper types (stubs are fine in bring-up, but they must define referenced static vars/constants).

Clean-room requirement: do not copy upstream compiler or tests into this repo; upstream is an untracked behavior oracle only.
acceptance_criteria: - bash scripts/hxhx/run-upstream-unit-macro-stage3-emit.sh progresses past TestNumericCasts (no Unbound module CastHelper).\n- Add a repo-local regression fixture (not copied from upstream) that declares a helper class in the same file with a referenced static var, and verify Stage3 emit+ocamlopt succeeds.\n- Document remaining limitations (typedef/enum/abstract in same module) and file follow-up beads where needed.

description:

  - array iteration via a tiny emitted OCaml shim (no hx runtime)
  - array literal/access + push + .length on the shim type
- Refresh packages/hxhx/bootstrap_out via scripts/hxhx/regenerate-hxhx-bootstrap.sh

Notes
- Keep MIT clean-room rules: no upstream code copying.
- Prefer adding/strengthening tests in scripts/test-hxhx-targets.sh once the snapshot is refreshed.

Prefer (1) short-term; keep stage0 as a local fallback but ensure CI/gate runners can enforce stage0-free.

title: Gate1: expression macro expansion rung
description: Upstream Gate1 uses expression macros heavily (e.g. unit.HelperMacros.getCompilationDate()) in normal code. A real compiler must execute these macros at compile time and splice the resulting AST.\n\nImplement an initial expression-macro expansion rung that can execute a small, allowlisted set of macro entrypoints (likely via the existing Stage4 macro host) and replace call sites with returned expressions.
design:

- Only support calls shaped like pack.Class.meth() and pack.Class.meth(<string literal>)

- Expansion occurs before typing
- Clean-room implementation: upstream is oracle-only via untracked vendor checkout
acceptance_criteria: - Can compile upstream-ish macro call sites like HelperMacros.getCompilationDate() when allowlisted\n- Limitations are documented; expansion is auditable (exact entrypoint strings)\n- Keep npm test green

Quality gates: npm run ci:guards + npm test pass.

title: Gate1: conditional compilation (#if) filtering for resolver
description: Our Stage3 resolver/parser currently ignores conditional compilation directives, so code inside #if blocks (e.g. java/cs/php targets) can be parsed and treated as active. This blocks any attempt to widen the module graph toward real Gate1, and can cause false import_missing failures (e.g. haxe.test.Base).\n\nImplement a minimal, provenance-safe conditional compilation pass that strips inactive blocks before parsing, using Stage3's define set (from -D plus builtin defines like sys/interp).
design:
Implement from scratch (do not port upstream):
- Support: #if <expr>, #elseif <expr>, #else, #end
- Expr subset: identifiers, !, &&, ||, parentheses, ident == "string", ident != "string"
- Define set: parsed -D name[=value] + implicit defines (sys/interp when --interp is present, etc.)
- For unknown identifiers, treat as false (conservative).
- Preserve line count where practical (optional) to keep errors readable.
acceptance_criteria: - Stage3 resolve/parse does not follow imports or type references in inactive #if branches\n- Gate1 bring-up can safely enable same-package type resolution without pulling java/cs/etc-only tests\n- Keep npm test green
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Marcelo Serpa
comments.text:
Progress: Stage3 now supports full statement-body emission for the bootstrap emitter via --hxhx-emit-full-bodies.

- Root cause: native frontend protocol v1 only captures headers/first-return (no bodies), so emitted OCaml bodies were empty.
- Fix: ParserStage now supports HIH_FORCE_HX_PARSER=1 to force the pure-Haxe parser even when -D hih_native_parser is compiled in.
- Stage3 sets HIH_FORCE_HX_PARSER=1 automatically when --hxhx-emit-full-bodies is used.
- Added/updated hxhx-target preset test to assert trace("HELLO") prints and is present in emitted Main.ml.

Quality: npm test (incl. test:hxhx-targets) passes.

comments.author: Marcelo Serpa
comments.text: Progress: native frontend now provides raw method bodies via ast method_body, enabling Stage3 full-body emission without forcing the pure-Haxe module parser (HIH_FORCE_HX_PARSER remains an override knob).

comments.author: Marcelo Serpa
comments.text:
Progress: Stage3 type-only now passes upstream tests/unit/compile-macro.hxml without stage0.

- `npm run test:upstream:unit-macro-stage3-typeonly` now succeeds end-to-end (resolve+type full graph; macros skipped by design).
- Runner now sets `HAXE_STD_PATH` from upstream checkout (`$UPSTREAM_DIR/std`) so it works with lix haxe shims.
- Typer improvements for upstream-shaped code:
  - normalize short type hints against module context (e.g. `Bytes` -> `haxe.io.Bytes`) to avoid false conflicts
  - treat “no explicit return statements” as `Unknown` (so explicit hints don’t conflict when bodies are skipped)
  - assignment unification failures widen locals to `Dynamic` instead of hard-failing (needed for generics like `IReport<Dynamic>`).

Next: start moving Stage3 from type-only to emit+build on a small upstream slice, then Stage4 real macro model + plugin ABI.

comments.author: Marcelo Serpa
comments.text: Progress: added Stage3 `--hxhx-no-emit` rung + upstream runner. This executes upstream `Macro.init()` + onGenerate hook and types the compile-macro graph without codegen, giving a Stage4+typer milestone before tackling the bootstrap emitter limitations.

comments.author: Marcelo Serpa
comments.text: Stage4 macro host: runtime haxe.macro.Context override now provides error/fatalError/warning/info/currentPos/getMessages stubs (avoids OCaml unused-var warning-as-error), and protocol doc clarifies current allowlist only supports no-arg calls. Also hardened Gate1 native runner to prefer upstream std via HAXE_STD_PATH. Verified: npm test + test:upstream:unit-macro-native.

comments.author: Marcelo Serpa
comments.text: Progress: Stage3 bootstrap emitter now fills omitted optional/default args for in-module calls (avoids OCaml partial-application type errors like Bytes.readString -> getString). Added upstream diagnostic runner: npm run test:upstream:unit-macro-stage3-emit (Stage3 emit+build+run) to validate macro host + OCaml emission wiring without stage0 delegation.

comments.author: Marcelo Serpa
comments.text: Progress: Stage4 macro host now supports builtin --macro include("Mod") (reverse RPC compiler.includeModule) and Stage3 resolver can take multiple roots (main + included modules). Added Stage3 bring-up test for include() affecting resolved_modules.

comments.author: Marcelo Serpa
comments.text:
Progress (2026-02-06): added reverse RPC method context.getBuildFields and compiler-side build-field snapshot payload (length-prefixed fragments), set per-module during Stage3 @:build execution. Documented in docs/02-user-guide/HXHX_MACRO_HOST_PROTOCOL.md.

Attempted Stage4 build-macro compatibility rung (Array<Field> return + delta emission), but blocked because compiling full haxe.macro.Expr (and related macro AST/types) to OCaml currently fails under dune (Lambda iterator typing + Expr displaykind; earlier also hit haxe.macro.Type naming). Reverted macro-host-side wiring for now to keep npm test green; leaving protocol+compiler snapshot in place for future work.

comments.author: Marcelo Serpa
comments.text:
Progress (2026-02-06): Stage3 bootstrap emitter now supports a small subset of boolean/int operators for meaningful control-flow in full-body mode.

- EmitterStage emits EBinop for +, comparisons (==, !=, <, <=, >, >=) and boolean ops (&&, ||), and EUnop for ! / - (still very limited).
- Updated scripts/test-hxhx-targets.sh full-body rung to assert if-conditions are not treated as always-true (prints OK, not BAD).

This is still far from Gate1 semantics (utest still stubbed by Obj.magic in stage3), but it removes a key false-positive behavior in bring-up tests.

comments.author: Marcelo Serpa
comments.text:
Progress (2026-02-06): strengthened native upstream Gate1 bring-up runner.

- scripts/hxhx/run-upstream-unit-macro-native.sh now uses --hxhx-no-emit (executes --macro Macro.init() + onGenerate) instead of --hxhx-type-only (which skipped macros).
- The script now asserts macro_run[0]=ok, hook_onGenerate[0]=ok, typed_modules=..., and stage3=no_emit_ok.

This is still a bring-up rung (no OCaml emission), but it is a closer oracle for Stage4 macro execution stability on upstream inputs.

This keeps the bring-up rung compiling+running further into utest sources without stage0, but it is still non-semantic (Obj.magic heavy) and not Gate1 acceptance yet.

Implemented Stage3 body parser coverage for parens, array literals/access, cast/untyped; regenerated packages/hxhx/bootstrap_out. Verified: npm test + npm run ci:guards + npm run test:upstream:unit-macro.

title: Gate1: macro host API parity for Macro.init + utest
description: Expand Stage4 macro host APIs beyond the current stub set to cover whatever upstream Macro.init() and the unit macro suite requires (Context.*, Compiler.*, hook lifecycles, error positions). Implement only what is required, but with a versioned, tested protocol.
acceptance_criteria:
- run-upstream-unit-macro-native.sh no longer needs Stage3 shortcuts for macro execution
- Macro errors include stable position payloads
- Add regression fixtures for each new macro API call (selftest + integration)
close_reason: Verified upstream Gate1 native attempt (compile-macro.hxml) runs Macro.init() successfully via Stage4 macro host (onGenerate+filterMessages no-op runtime override). Existing CI fixtures already cover define/getDefines hooks + error position payloads; no additional API gaps surfaced.

title: Gate1: OCaml --interp emulation for compile-macro.hxml (shim)
description: Add a shim-only OCaml "--interp" emulation path for Gate 1 bring-up: compile → native build → run. This validates reflaxe.ocaml’s dune build/run harness against upstream tests/unit/compile-macro.hxml while hxhx still delegates compilation to the stage0 haxe binary. The non-delegating swap (full native compiler pipeline) is tracked separately.
acceptance_criteria:
- hxhx supports --hxhx-ocaml-interp and --hxhx-ocaml-out <dir> to emulate --interp as build+run for OCaml
- Add scripts/hxhx/run-upstream-unit-macro-ocaml.sh that runs upstream tests/unit/compile-macro.hxml and executes the produced OCaml binary (skips gracefully if dune/ocamlc not installed)
- Document the OCaml --interp emulation and its current limitation (still stage0 shim)
- npm test passes
close_reason: Add shim-only OCaml --interp emulation (compile→build→run) via hxhx flags; add upstream runner script + npm alias; document Gate1 OCaml run mode; plus std/runtime parity fixes (Date getters + Bytes.fastGet) and snapshot updates.

title: Gate1: Stage3 typing for classes/modules (statics, fields, imports)
description: Extend the Stage3 typer from 'one main class' to upstream-shaped module typing: imported modules, static fields, instance fields, this/super, and basic classpath-based type lookup. This is needed for utest + upstream unit fixtures.
acceptance_criteria: - Fixture covers: imported static call, instance field access, this, basic constructor\n- Stage3 type-only on compile-macro.hxml reports typed_modules without escape hatches\n- New failures (if any) are about unimplemented features, not name resolution
close_reason: Stage3 now parses fields/this/new and types basic class/module surface via program index (imports, static calls, instance field/method access). Added Point/makePoint fixtures; updated hxhx stage3 runner and tests.

title: Gate1: Stage3 typer core (locals, unify, calls)
description: Implement a real Stage3 typer rung: local scopes, type inference/unification for primitives and functions, typing calls/field access, and structured error reporting with positions. Focus on features exercised by upstream tests/unit.
acceptance_criteria: - Add deterministic typer-summary output for fixtures (names + inferred types)\n- Type errors include file+line+col\n- Upstream Gate1 native runner progresses past parsing and fails on a *specific missing typer feature* (not generic crashes)
close_reason: Implemented Stage3 typer core: locals, unification, assignment/unary/binary typing, file+line+col TyperError; added deterministic root-module typer summary in stage3 --type-only; tests pass

title: Gate1: Stage3 parser support blocks + if/return + var/assign
description: Expand the Haxe-in-Haxe parser beyond signature-only so we can type real unit-test code: blocks, if/else, var declarations, assignments, and basic binary/unary expressions. This is the first rung toward a real typer (no more return-expr-only shortcuts).
acceptance_criteria: - Add/extend fixtures under examples/hih-compiler/fixtures exercising: block, if/else, var, assignment, simple arithmetic/comparisons\n- scripts/test-hxhx-targets.sh still passes\n- Stage3 can parse upstream tests/unit src enough to reach typing failures (not parser crashes)
close_reason: Parser now supports blocks/if/var/assign and basic unary/binary ops; fixtures updated; npm test passes

title: tests: stop depending on vendor/haxe for Macro.init fixture
description: scripts/test-hxhx-targets.sh currently builds the macro host with classpath vendor/haxe/tests/unit/src solely to access upstream Macro.init(). This breaks clean checkouts/CI that do not have vendor/haxe present. Add a local Macro.hx under examples/hxhx-macros and build against that instead.
acceptance_criteria:
- npm test passes in a repo checkout with no vendor/haxe directory
- scripts/test-hxhx-targets.sh still exercises Macro.init() hook registration
close_reason: Replace upstream Macro.init dependency with a local Macro.hx so npm test works without vendor/haxe.

title: hxhx(stage3): emit multi-module OCaml + support return call expressions
description: Stage3 currently types/emits only the root module and only supports return of literals/idents. Expand Stage3 so it can: (1) type all resolved modules (like type-only mode), (2) emit one OCaml compilation unit per resolved module (A.ml, Util.ml, ...), and (3) support emitting return expressions that are simple field/call chains (e.g. Util.ping()). This is a prerequisite rung toward upstream Gate1 (compile-macro.hxml).
acceptance_criteria: - scripts/test-hxhx-targets.sh Stage3 bring-up still passes\n- Extend Stage3 fixture to include a function returning a call expression (e.g. Util.ping()) and ensure build succeeds\n- npm test passes
close_reason: Closed

title: Gate2 runner: skip hxjava-dependent misc tests by default
description: Gate2 (runci Macro) currently triggers a network install of hxjava via tests/misc/projects/Issue11737/_setup.hxml (it runs --cmd haxelib install hxjava). For CI + offline-friendly bring-up, default to skipping that fixture unless explicitly enabled.
acceptance_criteria: - npm run test:upstream:runci-macro does not run Issue11737 by default (no hxjava install cmd)\n- Provide HXHX_GATE2_SKIP_HXJAVA=0 to re-enable the fixture\n- Document the skip in the runner header comments
close_reason: Closed

title: hxhx: resolve wildcard imports by trimming to base module
description: Stage1 and ResolverStage currently skip wildcard imports (import X.*), which upstream uses heavily (e.g. unit.Test.*). Implement a bootstrap rule: if an import ends with .*, trim the suffix and treat it as an import of the base module X (parse/visit that module). Keep a warning only if the base module cannot be resolved. Add a regression test in scripts/test-hxhx-targets.sh.
close_reason: Closed

title: hxhx(stage1): parse+resolve upstream compile-macro.hxml (non-shim)
description: Add an internal Stage1 permissive flag (for bring-up only) so Stage1 can accept upstream-ish flags and resolve -lib classpaths via haxelib path. Add a runner script that cd's into vendor/haxe/tests/unit and runs: hxhx --hxhx-stage1 --hxhx-permissive compile-macro.hxml --no-output. This should succeed without delegating to stage0 haxe.
close_reason: Closed

title: hxhx: support toplevel main modules (function main with no class)
description: Upstream Gate1 uses --main unit.TestMain where TestMain.hx defines a toplevel function main(), not a class with static main. Extend the native frontend protocol + HxModuleDecl to carry a toplevel_main flag, update HxParser similarly, and relax Stage1 entrypoint validation so modules with toplevel main are accepted. Add a regression test in scripts/test-hxhx-targets.sh.
close_reason: Closed

title: hxhx(stage3): add --type-only + type full resolved graph (Gate1 diagnostics)
description: Stage3 currently types only the root module, which can yield false-positive success for upstream-ish runs (e.g. tests/unit/compile-macro.hxml). Add a Stage3 bring-up option (e.g. --hxhx-type-only / --hxhx-type-all) that: (1) resolves the transitive module graph, (2) runs TyperStage.typeModule for every resolved module (best-effort), (3) runs macro hooks if requested, and (4) exits without emitting/building. Update the upstream native attempt runner to use this mode so failures move from frontend crashes to later-stage typing gaps deterministically.
close_reason: Closed

title: HXHX native frontend: parse real Haxe module headers
description: The current native frontend hook is a stub protocol that crashes on real-world Haxe code (e.g. utest/Runner.hx). Upgrade the native frontend seam so `hxhx` can parse at least module headers (package/imports/type names) for upstream-scale codebases, using upstream Haxe OCaml lexer/parser as the source of truth.
acceptance_criteria: - Native frontend can parse utest/Runner.hx without throwing opaque <object> exceptions\n- Stage3 native Gate1 attempt (npm run test:upstream:unit-macro-native) resolves the unit module graph past utest parsing (next failure should be later-stage typing/analysis, not frontend crash)\n- Protocol versioning documented/updated in docs/02-user-guide/HXHX_NATIVE_FRONTEND_PROTOCOL.md
close_reason: Closed

title: Gate 2: pass upstream runci Macro target
description: Make stage1/stage4 `hxhx` (native OCaml binary) pass upstream `tests/runci` Macro target (`tests/runci/targets/Macro.hx`) without delegating to stage0 `haxe`. This includes display fixtures, sourcemaps, null safety, misc, threads, and sys (sys skipped on macOS unless forced, per workflow doc).

- `npm run test:upstream:runci-macro` runs using stage1 `hxhx` in native mode (not the stage0 shim)
- Macro runci target passes on Linux baseline
- macOS runner behavior matches docs (sys skipped unless forced)
- Any flakes addressed with deterministic runner knobs (documented)

comments.text: 2026-02-07: Stage3 body parser recovery now avoids silent truncation when encountering unsupported constructs that leave stray closing braces. HxParser.parseFunctionBodyStatementsBestEffort treats only the wrapper close brace (followed by EOF) as end-of-body; other } are consumed and we emit EUnsupported placeholders (body_parse_error/stray_rbrace). comments.author: Marcelo Serpa
comments.text: 2026-02-07: Native frontend now supports multi-class modules deterministically when caller provides expected main class (new hook: parse_module_decl_with_expected). ParserStage passes expectedMainClass (file basename) into native hooks; Stage1 now forwards file paths into ParserStage.parse for main+imports. Native class parser also now skips class headers (extends/implements/generics/etc) before '{' so we don't silently drop methods. Added Stage1 regression in scripts/test-hxhx-targets.sh: multi-class module selects expected class. This should unblock runci modules like tests/runci/System.hx (CommandFailure then System).

comments.author: Marcelo Serpa
comments.text: 2026-02-07: Stage3 full-body emitter: exprToOcamlString now supports ternary + string concat (ETernary + EBinop '+') and passes through String-typed idents, so runci/System.hx successMsg/infoMsg no longer print '<unsupported>' when RunCi is emitted+run. Added Stage3 regression in scripts/test-hxhx-targets.sh: string ternary in Sys.println emits and runs (>hello<).

comments.author: Marcelo Serpa
comments.text: 2026-02-07: Stage3 now supports multi-unit .hxml via upstream-style --next/--each (bootstrap: --each treated like --next). title: Codegen: coerce if-branches for nullable primitives
description:
Haxe lowers 'a ?? b' into an if-expression whose overall type is non-nullable but whose then-branch may remain typed as Null<T> (flow-typed). Our OCaml codegen currently emits a raw OCaml if, which requires both branches to have the same type, so these patterns fail for Null<Int>/Null<Float>/Null<Bool>.

Reference: upstream Haxe typed AST dump for Null<Int> shows: if (tmp != null) tmp else 2 has overall type Int, then-branch type Null<Int>.
acceptance_criteria:

title: Restore Neko split-mode reachability for enum-abstract helper methods
description:
The full Neko native-backend smoke test currently reaches its later split-output check without the expected generated symbol for the enum-abstract helper Main.getNdllSuffix. The observed diagnostic is: expected enum abstract helper method to stay reachable in split mode, with Main_getNdllSuffix missing from the generated symbol table. Earlier focused assertions in the same run, including the new null-safe macro mapping check, completed before this independent failure.

Why this matters:
Split output places generated functions in separate Neko modules. If reachability analysis drops a helper that a retained method calls, the generated program can compile incompletely or fail at runtime. The smoke gate should be green and should explain which declaration caused each retained symbol.

First step:
Reproduce the failure from the exact committed baseline without the null-safe parser work, then minimize it to one enum abstract, one helper method, and one retained caller. Determine whether the defect is current baseline behavior, stale generated output, or a reachability regression. Do not make the helper globally reachable merely to satisfy the source-shape assertion.

Acceptance criteria:
1. A minimal fixture reproduces the missing helper with split output and proves whether non-split output differs.
2. Reachability records the exact call edge from the retained caller to the enum-abstract helper.
3. Generated split output contains the helper once and references the correct symbol; unused helpers remain removable.
4. The focused fixture executes when the Neko toolchain is available.
5. The full Neko native-backend smoke passes without weakening its assertion.
6. Ordinary class, static helper, abstract instance helper, and dead-helper controls remain green.
7. README Goals and North Star claims are reviewed without increasing readiness for an internal gate repair.

title: Route native macro-host builds through the shared heavy-run lease
description:
The native macro-host API test can trigger a fresh reflaxe.ocaml and OCaml build without first acquiring the user-scoped Haxe-family heavy-run lease. During haxe_ocaml-1x4rr verification, that build ran for about three and a half minutes at the same time as a leased Reflaxe.Ruby full suite. Both commands progressed, but the uncoordinated native build increased contention and extended the ordinary feedback loop.

Why this matters:
The project uses one shared lease across Haxe-family repositories because concurrent compiler generation, oversized emitter processing, and native builds have previously hung or starved each other. A test that reaches the same expensive build path outside that lease reopens the failure mode and makes measured latency unreliable.

Expected change:
Inventory the entry points used by the macro-host API and native module-host tests. Put the expensive build boundary behind the existing shared wrapper, while allowing nested callers that already own the lease to reuse it without deadlocking. Keep lightweight Haxe-only assertions outside the lease when they do not invoke native generation. The wrapper must not change the tested command or correctness result.

Acceptance criteria:
1. A focused fixture proves that a native macro-host build waits behind a peer repository owner instead of running concurrently.
2. The same test runs immediately when no owner exists and reuses an inherited owner when nested.
3. Timeout, child cleanup, build-directory cleanup, and exit-code forwarding remain deterministic.
4. The macro-host runtime API and native module-host ABI tests pass in both direct and nested-leased routes.
5. Before-and-after timings record cold and reusable macro-host paths, including time spent queued separately from build time.
6. The ordinary focused macro test loop does not acquire the heavy lease unless it actually reaches the expensive native build.
7. Documentation and README Goals are reviewed; this workflow repair does not increase product readiness by itself.

title: Lower null-safe field and call access across active backends
description:
The shared parser now keeps Haxe null-safe access, such as value?.copy(), distinct from an ordinary field read. JavaScript can emit this directly with optional chaining. OCaml, C++, Neko, and other active target paths still need a shared, behavior-correct lowering before they can execute the full syntax family.

Why this matters:
A null-safe access must evaluate its receiver in Haxe's required order and must not read the field or call the method when that receiver is null. An effectful receiver such as nextValue()?.run() must not be evaluated twice. Treating ?. as an ordinary dot would silently change program behavior, so the current parser slice deliberately preserves the distinction and unsupported emitters fail before generating wrong target code.

Expected design:
Use the structural typed body as the source of truth. Shared lowering should make the receiver evaluation, null test, selected field or call, result value, and nullable result type explicit before backend emission. Each backend should then emit that already-decided structure with target-native constructs where sound. Do not reparse source text, infer null safety from generated carrier types, or add target-local duplicate-evaluation rules.

Acceptance criteria:
1. Upstream Haxe 4.3.7 oracle fixtures cover null and non-null receivers, field reads, method calls, chained access, value position, and an effectful receiver with observable evaluation counts.

title: Stop repeated heavy-run waiting logs when only heartbeat age changes
description:
The user-scoped heavy-run scheduler should print a waiting message when the owner changes or when the wait begins, not every two-second heartbeat. During the current-source hxhx build for haxe_ocaml-1x4rr, an unchanged Reflaxe.Ruby owner caused repeated identical waiting lines. The comparison currently uses the complete lease summary, including heartbeatAgeMs, so the signature changes even though the owner and scheduling state do not.

Why this matters:
Repeated lines hide useful compiler output, make long gates harder to review, and waste log storage. The lease itself continued to serialize expensive work correctly; this issue is about dependable, quiet developer tooling.

Expected change:
Compare only stable scheduling facts such as status, reason, owner PID/start identity, label, and repository. Keep heartbeat age available for diagnostics, but do not use it to decide whether to repeat the ordinary waiting line. If a periodic progress message is desired, give it an explicit, much longer interval and label it as a progress update.

Acceptance criteria:
1. A focused test advances heartbeat age while keeping the same active owner and observes exactly one ordinary waiting line.
2. A change of owner or lease state produces a new line.
3. Timeout, stale-owner recovery, nested reuse, signal forwarding, and lease release behavior remain unchanged.
4. The local queued workflow remains deterministic and does not add sleep-heavy tests.
5. Documentation and README Goals are reviewed; no readiness increase is implied by this log-quality repair.
close_reason: The heavy-run wrapper now suppresses duplicate wait lines caused only by heartbeat age while preserving real state changes; focused, capacity, and cross-repository lease fixtures pass.
