Preserve the distinction between an explicit source annotation and a semantic inferred type. Keep target carrier selection in extracted C++ inference/model seams, and keep semantic types in shared typed nodes. Do not hard-code TestBasetypes, h_2, IntMap, std::any, or String-array text; do not blanket-delete useful typed local evidence or move map semantics into the backend.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Add a repo-owned regression with two sequential locals sharing one Haxe name: an explicitly parameterized IntMap followed by new IntMap() whose set value is an Array<String>. 2) Typed-body evidence proves inferred-source annotation state and lexical declaration identity survive projection, while generated C++ uses an explicitly parameterized or auto IntMap<Array<String>> carrier and never a bare IntMap or std::any fallback. 3) Explicit map annotations, StringMap/IntMap primitive values, scoped branches, redeclared map-key vectors, Map literals, generic arrays, and ordinary local redeclarations remain green. 4) Formatter, typed-body, full C++ native smoke, map controls, mega-file and relevant guards pass. 5) A fresh stage0-forbidden, zero-retry, unchanged-timeout C++ Gate3 removes this error and records the next independent first failure. 6) CI, provenance, bootstrap snapshot impact, cleanup, README Goals, and North Star review are recorded honestly.

Keep source-language type identities distinct even when their short names collide, and use deterministic generated names. Do not special-case this fixture or rename upstream standard-library declarations in parsed source.

title: Core: index abstract operators with canonical semantic identities
description: Build the shared semantic catalog needed to recognize Haxe abstract operators before any backend emits them. Add deterministic nominal type and declaration identities, keep primitive-backed abstracts semantically distinct from their underlying carriers, model abstracts as TyAbstractInfo beside TyClassInfo, and parse unary @:op metadata once into TyperIndex. This bead establishes declaration loading and deterministic diagnostics only; it does not bind operator expressions, lower mutation, change C++ carriers, or introduce a compiler-wide IR.
design: Adopt the corrected 2026-07-15 GPT-5.5 Pro abstract-operator review. This bead follows haxe_ocaml-4vf5p so the catalog keys use the structured unary token/fixity. Stable identity means deterministic structural identity such as canonical owner plus declaration discriminator; it does not require unstable allocation-order integers. Keep parser source declarations as provenance, but semantic lookup must use the shared catalog.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Canonical nominal type identities are deterministic across identical builds and include type arguments where supported; display strings are diagnostic text, not binding keys. 2) Abstract declarations produce TyAbstractInfo and retain their underlying semantic type without being treated as ordinary classes. 3) Shared declaration records retain stable identity, signature, metadata, body reference, source position when available, and static/instance/inline status. 4) Unary @:op metadata is parsed and validated once into an operator catalog reachable through TyperIndex; arbitrary helper names work and ordinary classes gain no operator behavior. 5) Malformed and duplicate metadata diagnostics are deterministic. 6) Focused semantic dumps/tests, formatter, current-source validation, bootstrap equivalence, provenance guards, README Goals review, and North Star review pass. 7) No backend metadata scan or operator selection is added.

Enum-abstract member retention remains explicitly tracked by haxe_ocaml-g7gyg.

title: Core: carry structural typed function bodies into every backend
description: Give hxhx a durable place to store semantic expression decisions. Introduce a structurally recursive typed-body spine in TypedModule and switch active backends to consume typed function bodies instead of re-reading parsed function bodies. This is a core typed semantic tree, not a target-neutral GenIR. Parsed declarations remain available for imports, metadata, diagnostics, source provenance, and macro quotation; parsed bodies must no longer drive semantic emission.
design: Split from the external review's combined catalog-and-typed-body bead because current backends contain widespread parsed-declaration access and the semantic body cutover is independently large. Depend on the canonical identity/catalog bead. GenIrProgram remains an alias; do not invent backend normalization or a binding side table. A guard must distinguish legitimate parsed declaration/provenance reads from forbidden parsed function-body emission.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Every body-bearing function in TypedModule has a structural typed body whose nested expressions cannot hide bindable operators or mutations in opaque leaves. 2) Typed nodes carry semantic type, exact declaration references for calls, and the best available source position; missing nested positions are explicit rather than fabricated. 3) The node set supports ordinary expressions, exact calls, blocks/sequences, temporary locals, reads, writes, assignments, and unary operations. 4) All active backends consume typed bodies for semantic emission in one API cutover while ordinary generated behavior remains equivalent. 5) A repository guard forbids backend reads of parsed function bodies without banning parsed declaration/provenance access. 6) Program revision/lifecycle rules prevent post-typing parsed-body mutation from silently invalidating typed bodies. 7) Focused cross-backend tests, typed-body invariant scans, formatter, current-source validation, allowlisted bootstrap regeneration/equivalence, provenance guards, README Goals review, and North Star review pass.

title: Preserve prefix/postfix increment syntax through every hxhx backend
description: The parser currently rewrites source prefix increment/decrement into compound assignment while postfix remains an EUnop form. Haxe abstracts may declare distinct @:op(++x), @:op(x++), and @:op(A += B) helpers, so this loses semantics before typing. Make a hard cutover that preserves operator spelling and fixity through the shared expression model, then update every active consumer in one coherent slice: ordinary operator emission, assigned-local and mutability discovery, macro quoting/conversion, diagnostics, tests, and required bootstrap snapshots. This bead owns syntax identity and ordinary operator compatibility only; it does not claim abstract-helper selection or invent target-local metadata resolution.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Original parser tests distinguish prefix, postfix, and compound-assignment AST shapes for increment and decrement. 2. Every active backend that consumes HxExpr emits or lowers ordinary prefix/postfix increment and decrement correctly; no backend prints an internal operator tag as source. 3. Assigned-local, mutability, capture, inference, and diagnostic traversals recognize both fixities. 4. Runtime macro conversion and target macro quoting preserve haxe.macro.Expr EUnop operator plus postFix in both directions, with focused round-trip coverage. 5. Existing postfix and compound-assignment behavior remains green across JS, Neko, C++, OCaml/bootstrap, and source-native focused lanes. 6. Official formatter, focused tests, current-source validation, required snapshot regeneration/equivalence, and relevant guards pass. 7. The bead records the exact consumer inventory and next abstract-binding dependency; it makes no claim that @:op dispatch is implemented. 8. title: Clarify Reflaxe source stdPaths vs CompilerInit wiring
description: Why: after checking haxe.rust and the generated Reflaxe newproject template, the docs should state the simpler convention precisely: source dev/test entrypoints put stdPaths, including _std, on the initial classpath before typing; CompilerInit.Start only registers/configures the compiler and should not be described as the _std compatibility injection point. What: tighten reflaxe.ocaml README and cross/_std guide so haxelib dev is clearly a temporary checkout override, raw package-source dev is not the recommended path, and package builds remain the Reflaxe flattening path to .cross.hx.
notes:
Checked the generated Reflaxe template in ../haxe.compilerdev.reference/reflaxe/newproject: haxelib.json declares reflaxe.stdPaths ["std", "std/LANG/_std"], extraParams.hxml only defines target flags and calls langcompiler.CompilerInit.Start(), and CompilerInit.Start() only registers ReflectCompiler.AddCompiler. It does not add _std with Compiler.addClassPath.

Checked ../haxe.rust: source std overrides live under std/rust/_std, haxe_libraries/reflaxe.rust.hxml supplies std/rust/_std before typing for source-mode builds, and scripts/release/package-haxelib.sh delegates package flattening to Reflaxe Run build so _std becomes packaged .cross.hx. Rust has a CompilerBootstrap macro for vendored Reflaxe/std support assets, but its docs explicitly say source-checkout std overrides must be supplied before typing and not rescued by macro-time _std injection. Current checkout has no checked-in .cross.hx under src/ or std.

Docs updated to state the simpler convention: source/test entrypoints own initial _std classpath visibility; package builds own _std-to-.cross.hx flattening; CompilerInit.Start() registers/configures the compiler and should not be described as the _std compatibility mechanism. Also clarified haxelib dev as a temporary repo-root checkout override, not the normal external workflow, and corrected the family Rust audit/matrix rows.

title: Cpp Type.ValueType carriers need real discriminants for Type.typeof equality
description: haxe_ocaml-ibypk introduces a bounded __hxhx_value_type_eq seam so Type.enumEq(Type.typeof(v), rt) compiles when Type.typeof lowers to a string type name and rt is a generated Type_ValueType carrier. notes: Implemented bounded Cpp ValueType carrier semantics for Type.typeof comparisons. First visible hard errors start near TestMain.cpp:4519 with `Iterator` not declared/template argument invalid, then EnumValueMap/BalancedTree surface errors such as missing BalancedTree base/member support and EnumValue helper methods. Diagnose and implement the narrow Cpp-native iterator/map surface needed to move this first blocker without adding broad fake runtime stubs.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Capture the run 27870512248 first-error shape at behavior level without vendoring upstream tests. 2) Add focused Cpp smoke/regression coverage for the minimal Iterator/haxe.ds map surface observed. 3) Implement the narrow target-owned Cpp support/lowering/extraction seam; avoid growing SourceTargetCommon or CppTargetCore with large inline fake runtime classes unless a small temporary helper is explicitly justified and tracked. 4) Preserve prior Cpp Full1 burn-down fixes, including NativeString/ConstPointer and ArraySort helper signatures. 5) Run focused Cpp smoke, formatter, bootstrap regen/build if compiler source changes, git diff --check, guard:hx-format, ci:guards, cleanup. 6) Rerun focused remote Gate3 Full1 Cpp and verify it advances past the Iterator/map first blocker or record/split the next blocker. 7) Record docs/README Goals table review outcome; update only if production-readiness, public workflows, CI contracts, or release scope changed.
close_reason: Focused remote Gate3 Cpp run 27879139573 advanced past the Iterator/haxe.ds map, BalancedTree, and EnumValueMap first-error surfaces tracked by this bead; the next first blocker is a distinct Timer/MainLoop/sys-thread event runtime surface tracked as haxe.ocaml-cpp-timer-mainloop-runtime-surface.

comments.author: Marcelo Serpa
comments.text:
Checkpoint: first bounded SourceTargetCommon extraction.

Inventory by concern:
- Shared AST/source rendering: expression/statement/class emission, name normalization, target dispatch glue.
- Target-specific lowering: PHP/C#/Java/Lua/Python syntax and runtime semantics currently mixed into the shared file.
- Runtime/template emission: generated support classes/functions, helper bodies, and target-specific compatibility glue.
- Target intrinsics/externs: platform APIs and syntax constructs that should usually live as extern/core declarations, templates, support modules, or intrinsic lowering instead of inline emitter stubs.
- Parser/scanner compensation: temporary metadata and scan-stage repairs used by source-native bootstrap gaps.
- Test-harness compatibility shims: targeted Full1/gate burn-down repairs that should not become permanent architecture gravity.

Target-owned layout proposal:
- Keep SourceTargetCommon as the shared dispatcher plus truly common rendering helpers.
- Move target-owned families into backend.source.<Target>* modules, starting with PHP because current Full1 burn-down is hitting PHP seams.
- Use upstream Haxe 4.3.7 generator ownership only as an architecture reference: target generators are separate files with shared support separated. No upstream compiler code or tests copied.
- Extraction order: PHP abstract/runtime helpers, PHP syntax/intrinsics, then C#/Java/Lua/Python helper families; templates/support modules should replace large inline string bodies where the surface is runtime/extern-like.
- Guardrail: if a SourceTargetCommon touch starts expanding a target-specific family or large inline out.push block, extract/design the boundary before adding more.

Implemented in this slice:
- Extracted PHP abstract facade method merging into backend.source.PhpAbstractFacadeSupport.

title: R&D: source-native runtime packaging and extern strategy
description:
R&D follow-up from PHP Gate3 burn-down and SourceNativeBackend architecture review: SourceTargetCommon/SourceTargetCommon-generated target runtimes are accumulating large inline target runtime shims via lines.push. Investigate whether source-native runtime packaging should move to dedicated runtime modules/templates, checked-in generated runtime assets, or a limited extern/__php__-style strategy for target-native helpers.

The explicit question to answer: where are lines.push runtime fragments justified as compiler-owned glue, and where should we instead model target helpers as runtime externs/native snippets with typed Haxe-facing APIs? The review should include PHP first and then scan adjacent source-native targets/runtime surfaces for the same smell.

The goal is better architecture, testability, and reviewability without reintroducing stage0 dependency, target-backend coupling, large generated artifacts, or provenance risk. Related prior architecture bead haxe.ocaml-sssk.41 extracted SourceNativeBackend target ownership boundaries; this task should build on that instead of reopening the same split.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Inventory current inline runtime emission surfaces in SourceTargetCommon and target-specific source-native backends, especially PHP lines.push helpers. 2) Classify each surface as justified compiler-owned generated glue, runtime-library helper, extern/__php__ candidate, or target-template asset. 3) Compare at least three approaches: keep inline emitters but extract typed modules/templates; checked-in generated/runtime assets; extern/__php__-style runtime sources with Haxe-facing APIs. 4) Document constraints around stage0-free source-native builds, bootstrap snapshots, artifact size, CI cache shape, provenance/licensing, and target-backend coupling. 5) Include adjacent source-native target/runtime areas, not only PHP, and note whether the architecture should stay close to upstream behavior or intentionally diverge. 6) Produce a recommended migration plan with small implementation beads, dependencies, and priority ordering. 7) README Goals status/docs review recorded at checkpoint.

title: Expose reflaxe.elixir as an official native hxhx target surface after native readiness
description:
User direction (2026-03-18): once reflaxe.elixir is proven native-ready, integrate it into hxhx as an official native target surface. The first supported surface may be plugin/host-adapter based if that is the supported native path, but the outcome must be presented as a real native hxhx target story rather than only an external pilot.

Scope:
- define the supported user-facing native invocation(s) for reflaxe.elixir under hxhx
- prefer the currently proven plugin/host-adapter path unless the architecture later widens to builtin integration
- document whether builtin support is deferred, experimental, or out of scope
- add proof commands/artifacts that show reflaxe.elixir compiling and working through the supported native hxhx path

Acceptance criteria:
1. A documented official native hxhx surface exists for reflaxe.elixir (plugin/host-adapter or builtin), with exact commands.
2. The supported path compiles a real reflaxe.elixir workload and records runnable proof artifacts.
3. Docs/matrix language no longer leaves reflaxe.elixir as merely an external pilot once this path is green.
4. If builtin integration is not the chosen first-class path, that is stated explicitly with rationale and follow-up tracking.
close_reason: Docs now name the official native hxhx surface for reflaxe.elixir as the plugin-hosted path, with exact commands, proof artifacts, and explicit statement that builtin is a later graduation path rather than a prerequisite for officiality.

title: Verify native-compiled reflaxe-elixir against repo tests and todo-app QA after compile success
description:
Once the official native `hxhx + reflaxe.ocaml -> plugin` compile lane succeeds on reflaxe-elixir, run the real reflaxe-elixir validation harness instead of stopping at compile/build artifacts.

Scope:
- repo root: `vendor/reflaxe-elixir`
- verify the compiled/native path against the repo test and QA entrypoints
- compare failures against the upstream-host baseline before changing semantics

Primary harness entrypoints discovered locally:
- repo suite: `npm test`
- repo guards: `npm run ci:guards`
- repo runtime smoke: `npm run test:runtime-smoke`
- repo mix test lane: `npm run test:mix`
- todo-app Haxe-authored ExUnit compile: `scripts/with-timeout.sh --secs 180 --cwd examples/todo-app -- haxe build-tests.hxml`
- todo-app ExUnit: `scripts/with-timeout.sh --secs 420 --cwd examples/todo-app -- mix test`
- todo-app QA sentinel: `scripts/qa-sentinel.sh --app examples/todo-app --port 4001 --async --deadline 600 --verbose`
- todo-app full Playwright suite: `scripts/qa-sentinel.sh --app examples/todo-app --env e2e --port 4001 --playwright --e2e-spec "e2e/*.spec.ts" --async --deadline 900 --verbose`

Notes:
- Use the native-compiled reflaxe-elixir artifact that actually passed the official native compile proof, not an older bootstrap binary.
- Treat upstream `haxe + reflaxe.ocaml` results as the behavioral baseline.
- Capture which failures are compiler/codegen issues versus app/env/tooling issues.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A native-compiled reflaxe-elixir artifact is run against the real repo harness, not just a reduced smoke.
2. Results are recorded for `npm test`, `npm run ci:guards`, and the todo-app test/QA flows.
3. Failures are triaged into compiler/codegen vs environment/app issues with artifact/log references.
4. Any remaining gaps are turned into narrower follow-up beads.
notes: Starting real reflaxe-elixir harness verification now that the official native compile proof lanes are green. First step is to inspect the repo harness and map each entrypoint to the native artifact/host path we can actually exercise.
close_reason: Closed after the native verifier recorded npm-test, ci:guards, and todo-app test/QA flows with retained artifacts, officialNativePath remained pass, and remaining failures were narrowed to explicit diagnostic source-host follow-up beads.

title: Family hardening: fail fast on mixed Reflaxe target activation
description:

This task covers the early `packages/reflaxe.ocaml/src/haxe/*.cross.hx` ownership set (`haxe.Exception`, `haxe.NativeStackTrace`, `haxe.ValueException`) and the interaction with sibling targets. Canonical references live in this repo:
- `docs/02-user-guide/CROSS_AND_STAGED_STDLIB_GUIDE.md`
- `docs/00-project/REFLAXE_FAMILY_CROSS_OVERRIDE_AUDIT.md`
- `docs/00-project/REFLAXE_FAMILY_CROSS_OVERRIDE_MATRIX.md`
Use those docs as the source of truth for rationale, overlap surfaces, and acceptable scope; do not re-derive the family model from scratch in implementation.
acceptance_criteria:
- Add explicit mixed-target detection or fail-fast behavior when sibling Reflaxe target libraries are active in one compilation and OCaml early override ownership would become ambiguous.
- Keep the current OCaml bootstrap model (`std/` always, `std/_std` only for OCaml) intact.
- Document any intentionally retained early `.cross.hx` exceptions and why they cannot move to `_std` yet.
- Add or update at least one focused smoke/regression test if a deterministic mixed-activation shape is practical.
close_reason: Deferred: no current product need for same-compilation sibling Reflaxe target activation; reopen if mixed-target activation becomes a real supported workflow.

title: Replace Stage3 backend reflective emit fallback with typed dispatch
description:
Problem
- `packages/hxhx/src/hxhx/Stage3Compiler.hx` still has a reflective fallback in `emitWithBackend`:
  - `Reflect.field(backendReflect, "emit")`
  - `Reflect.callMethod(...)`
- This seam is currently justified as a bootstrap compatibility boundary, but it keeps `Dynamic`/reflection on a correctness-critical path and weakens static guarantees.

Goal
- Remove (or strictly eliminate in default paths) the reflective backend emit fallback by moving to typed backend dispatch contracts for dynamic/bundled providers.

Scope
1) Define typed fallback contract for backend emit dispatch that works in Stage3 bootstrap lane.
2) Replace reflective emit lookup/invoke in `Stage3Compiler.emitWithBackend` with typed dispatch through boundary helpers.
3) Keep compatibility with existing builtin backends and dynamic provider loading semantics.
4) Keep any unavoidable boundary cast isolated in one helper with guardrails.
5) Add/update tests and docs for dispatch policy.

Acceptance criteria

title: Stage3 backend providers: remove reflective registrations path
description:
Problem
- Stage3 currently loads dynamic backend providers by reflecting a static `providerRegistrations()` method from `Type.resolveClass(typePath)` and casting the returned value.
- This keeps `Reflect.callMethod` + array casts on a critical selection path and weakens type safety (especially with our Any/Dynamic minimization policy).

Goal
- Keep provider loading behavior-compatible while tightening typing and reducing reflection usage.

Scope
1) Add a compile-time known-provider table for builtin provider entrypoints (starting with `backend.js.JsBackend`) so known paths avoid reflection entirely.
2) For non-builtin providers, switch from static reflective method calls to typed instance loading:
   - `Type.resolveClass(typePath)` + `Type.createInstance(cls, [])`
   - require `ITargetBackendProvider` and call `registrations()`
   - fail fast with actionable errors if type missing, ctor invalid, or interface not implemented.
3) Keep deterministic registration order and tracing behavior unchanged.
4) Add regression coverage for:
   - known provider path
   - custom provider implementing `ITargetBackendProvider`
   - negative cases (type missing / wrong interface).

Design notes / alternatives
- Option A (preferred now): static provider table + typed instance providers.
  Pros: simple, no macro complexity, immediate type-safety gain, minimal churn.
  Cons: builtin provider table must be maintained manually.
- Option B: macro-generated provider registry (scan known providers at build time).
  Pros: less manual table upkeep.

5) Update OCaml Stage3 stmt handling to compile safely with the new nodes (no pattern-match gaps).
6) Remove now-redundant js-native marker special-casing for break/continue.

title: backend boundary follow-up: centralize GenIrProgram recovery cast helper
description:
Context
- We currently use `requireProgram(program:GenIrProgram):GenIrProgram { return cast program; }` in:
  - `packages/hih-compiler/src/backend/js/JsTargetCore.hx`
  - `packages/hih-compiler/src/backend/ocaml/OcamlTargetCore.hx`
- This cast is currently justified because reflaxe/OCaml dispatch can degrade `ITargetCore.emit` parameters to `Obj.t` at generated OCaml interface boundaries.
- Without boundary recovery, Stage0 build fails in generated ML with type mismatch:
  - `program has type Obj.t but expected MacroExpandedProgram.t`.

Problem
- The cast is correct today, but duplicated in multiple target cores.
- Duplicated boundary recovery logic increases drift risk and obscures where dynamic recovery is allowed.
- We need one canonical, documented boundary policy that survives backend growth (js/ocaml and future promoted targets).

Goal
- Centralize `GenIrProgram` boundary recovery in one shared helper/pattern.
- Keep target-core emitters fully typed and free of ad-hoc boundary casts.
- Preserve current behavior and Stage0 build stability.

Scope
1) Design a shared helper for boundary recovery (single location, minimal surface).
2) Migrate `JsTargetCore` and `OcamlTargetCore` to the shared helper.
3) Define explicit policy for where boundary casts are allowed vs forbidden.
4) Add a targeted regression check that would fail if boundary recovery is removed or drifted.
5) Document the final pattern in backend architecture docs.

Proposed Implementation (candidate)
- Add one utility under backend layer, e.g. `packages/hih-compiler/src/backend/GenIrBoundary.hx`:
  - `public static inline function requireProgram(program:GenIrProgram):GenIrProgram`.
- Replace local `requireProgram(...)` duplicates in target cores with helper call.
- Keep any unavoidable casts at Stage3 reflection/provider seams explicitly documented.

Constraints
- No upstream code copying; keep MIT clean-room workflow.
- No behavior change in backend output.
- Keep changes minimal and reviewable.

Risk/Tradeoffs
- Over-aggressive refactor could destabilize Stage3 bootstrap.
- Keeping duplicates invites divergence when additional target cores land.

Validation
- `haxe -cp packages/hxhx/src -cp packages/hih-compiler/src -cp packages/reflaxe.ocaml/src -cp packages/reflaxe.ocaml/std -main hxhx.Main --no-output -D hih_native_parser`
- `npm run -s test:hxhx:builtin-target-smoke`
- If available in same session: a Stage0 bootstrap build proving no `Obj.t` vs `MacroExpandedProgram.t` regression in generated ML.

Notes
- This is follow-up technical debt after boundary hardening work in `haxe.ocaml-3b7`.
- Priority intentionally set to later (not blocker) because current casts are correct and localized.
acceptance_criteria: 1) A shared backend boundary helper exists and is used by both JsTargetCore and OcamlTargetCore instead of duplicated local requireProgram helpers. 2) Cast policy is documented: allowed only at explicit boundary seams; forbidden in core emitter logic. 3) Compile + smoke validation pass (native parser no-output + builtin target smoke). 4) At least one bootstrap/generated-ML validation note is recorded showing no Obj.t vs MacroExpandedProgram.t regression.
notes: Implemented central boundary helper packages/hih-compiler/src/backend/GenIrBoundary.hx and migrated JsTargetCore/OcamlTargetCore to it. Added explicit Stage3 backend-dispatch seam handling so reflaxe OCaml output no longer regresses Obj.t vs MacroExpandedProgram at the emit bridge boundary (validated with HXHX_FORCE_STAGE0=1 HXHX_STAGE0_FAILFAST_SECS=1200 bash scripts/hxhx/build-hxhx.sh). Also validated native parser compile smoke and full target workflow (HXHX_BIN=packages/hxhx/out/_build/default/out.bc npm run -s test:hxhx-targets).

title: backend boundary: eliminate GenIrProgram cast leakage
description:
Context
- During `hxhx` Stage3/backend integration, `ITargetCore.emit(program, context)` is typed in Haxe as `program:GenIrProgram`.
- In generated OCaml for dynamic backend dispatch, `program` can degrade to `Obj.t` at the call boundary.
- We observed concrete failures in generated files (`backend_js_JsTargetCore.ml`, `backend_ocaml_OcamlTargetCore.ml`) when typed operations expected `MacroExpandedProgram.t`.
- Current fixes use local `cast` to recover type where needed. This is acceptable short-term but not ideal architecture.

Problem Statement
- The current boundary leaks dynamic typing into target-core implementation code.
- Casts can spread and become fragile, reducing readability and confidence in correctness.
- Generated OCaml type-checking errors can surface late (during bootstrap/build), not at earlier Haxe-check points.

Goal
- Define and implement a robust, explicit boundary strategy for `GenIrProgram` that:
  1) keeps current behavior working,
  2) centralizes dynamic->typed conversion,
  3) prevents cast proliferation,
  4) improves generated OCaml type stability,
  5) remains aligned with MIT clean-room goals (no upstream code copying).

Scope (this task)
1. Design review of 3 candidate approaches:
   - A) Single boundary adapter (`requireProgram(v:Dynamic):GenIrProgram`) used only at wrapper seams.
   - B) API refactor of backend dispatch to preserve static types (avoid reflective/dynamic return path where possible).
   - C) Replace `typedef GenIrProgram = MacroExpandedProgram` with a concrete wrapper type to enforce explicit conversion semantics.
2. Choose a preferred near-term implementation path and a medium-term roadmap.
3. Produce implementation checklist + risk analysis + migration order.
4. Identify required regression tests (Haxe-level and generated OCaml/build-level).
5. Document decision in repo docs (where architecture decisions for backend layering live).

Out of Scope
- Full backend architecture rewrite in one PR.
- Large unrelated refactors across parser/typer/runtime.

Deliverables
- Decision note with chosen approach and rationale.
- Concrete task breakdown for incremental rollout (small, reviewable PRs).
- Tests/gates mapping showing how we validate the boundary.
- Update docs to record the boundary contract and “where casts are allowed” policy.

Suggested Validation Matrix
- `npm run test:m14:target-core-wiring`
- `npm run test:m14:js-target-core-wiring`
- `npm run test:hxhx-targets` (or at minimum `scripts/hxhx/build-hxhx.sh` + js-native smoke lane)
- Any added focused regression test proving generated OCaml no longer fails due `Obj.t`/`MacroExpandedProgram.t` mismatches.

Risk Notes
- Overly aggressive refactor could destabilize Stage3 bring-up.
- Leaving design unresolved will continue causing late bootstrap failures and repeated tactical casts.
acceptance_criteria: A documented boundary decision exists with chosen approach and migration plan; casts are centralized to an explicit boundary helper/pattern (not spread through target cores); targeted wiring tests and at least one end-to-end build/smoke pass validate no Obj.t vs MacroExpandedProgram.t regressions; docs updated to define allowed cast boundary policy.
notes: Implemented near-term boundary decision (Approach B): keep backend and target-core emit APIs statically typed on GenIrProgram, remove local target-core program-cast helpers, and keep casts constrained to narrow Stage3 reflection/bridge seams. Updated docs with explicit policy and roadmap in docs/02-user-guide/HXHX_BACKEND_LAYERING.md and docs/02-user-guide/HXHX_BUILTIN_BACKENDS.md; README now references typed provider contract and cast policy. Validation passed: haxe -cp packages/hxhx/src -cp packages/hih-compiler/src -cp packages/reflaxe.ocaml/src -cp packages/reflaxe.ocaml/std -main hxhx.Main --no-output -D hih_native_parser; npm run -s test:hxhx:builtin-target-smoke.
close_reason: Closed

title: Stage3 emitter: model instance field reads/writes in full-body mode
description:
Why

- Stage3 emitter still lowers instance field reads/writes to bring-up poison (Obj.magic 0) because object layout is not modeled yet.

What

How
- Introduce a conservative instance field representation in generated units (or runtime shim) for classes used in Stage3 full-body mode.
- Handle this.x assignment and this.x access in exprToOcaml / statement lowering.
- Add regression that compile+run checks field roundtrip in full-body mode (currently no-emit strict check only).
acceptance_criteria:
- scripts/test-hxhx-targets.sh includes a compile+run regression where constructor writes this.x and method reads it
- regression prints expected value without Obj.magic 0 fallback for that path
- existing Stage3 target tests remain green

title: Stage3 emitter: haxe.Int64 bring-up for FPHelper
description:
Why
- Upstream stdlib code referenced by Gate2 (notably haxe.io.FPHelper) uses haxe.Int64 construction and mutators (ofInt/make/set_low/set_high).
- Stage3 emit-runner currently models haxe.Int64 as a small OCaml record (Haxe_Int64.t) but can still emit calls to OCaml's Int64 module or miss required helpers, causing OCaml compile failures before RunCi control-flow executes.

What
- Extend the Stage3 bootstrap emission path so the generated OCaml for stdlib modules can typecheck with our record-based haxe.Int64 model.
- Keep changes bring-up scoped: prefer small shims and targeted call rewrites over full Int64 semantics.

How
- Add/extend Haxe_Int64 shim functions needed by FPHelper (at least ofInt + make; likely also set_low/set_high or equivalent).
- Rewrite Int64.* call sites during emission to the shim (avoid OCaml Int64.* entirely in Stage3 output).
- Add a regression that compiles the Stage3 emitted Haxe_io_FPHelper module in the Gate2 stage3_emit_runner output graph.
acceptance_criteria: - Gate2 stage3_emit_runner no longer fails on haxe.io.FPHelper Int64 usage\n- Generated OCaml does not reference OCaml Int64.ofInt (or other camelCase Int64 names)\n- Local npm test remains green
close_reason: Closed

title: Chore: speed up hxhx bootstrap snapshot regen
description:
Investigate why stage0 snapshot regeneration for hxhx can take >10 minutes and appears to make no progress (packages/hxhx/out stays empty for a long time).

Goals
- Make scripts/hxhx/regenerate-hxhx-bootstrap.sh reliably complete on dev machines.
- Prefer stage0 emit-only + dune build verification (no redundant dune build inside stage0).
- Document a reliable stage0 Haxe invocation strategy (pin HAXE_BIN; avoid editor/shim server-connect surprises).

Ideas
- Add a verbose/profiling mode that runs stage0 haxe with --times and captures logs.
- Optionally support using a compilation server (haxe --wait / --connect) for faster local runs.
- Add a guard that kills stale stage0 haxe processes before starting regeneration.

Constraints
- Must preserve MIT clean-room rules (no vendoring upstream Haxe sources/tests).
acceptance_criteria:
- scripts/hxhx/regenerate-hxhx-bootstrap.sh completes in a bounded time on a clean repo
- The produced packages/hxhx/bootstrap_out builds with dune build
- Documented in packages/hxhx/README.md or scripts/hxhx/README.md (whichever is appropriate)

title: Gate1: lazy type-driven module loading
description: Stage3 currently only loads modules via explicit imports + a heuristic same-package scan. Real compilation needs type-driven loading: when the typer resolves an unknown type path, it should load the corresponding module from classpaths. This avoids brittle heuristics and is prerequisite for scaling beyond the current resolved_modules=24 bring-up rung.
design: Implement a ModuleLoader owned by Stage3: given classpaths + current package, resolve a type path to a module file, parse it, and insert into TyperIndex + worklist. Keep it deterministic and cycle-safe.
acceptance_criteria: - Typer can request/load modules on demand when it encounters unknown types\n- Works with conditional compilation filtering so inactive #if branches don't trigger loads\n- Keep npm test green

title: Stage4: remove stage0 dependency for building hxhx-macro-host
description: Gate1/Gate2 runners currently auto-build the macro host by invoking stage0 'haxe' via scripts/hxhx/build-hxhx-macro-host.sh when HXHX_MACRO_HOST_EXE is unset. This keeps Gate1 'native' bring-up from being truly stage0-free and complicates distribution.\n\nGoal: make macro-host availability stage0-free by default (prebuilt binary, or build via hxhx itself, or an alternate minimal host).
design:
Options (pick one):
1) Ship prebuilt macro-host binaries as release artifacts and have runners download/cache them (preferred for CI, but OS-specific).
2) Build macro host via hxhx Stage3 emitter + dune (requires Stage3 emitter to handle macro-host code subset).
3) Replace macro host with a minimal OCaml-only host for early rungs, keeping protocol the same.
acceptance_criteria: - Running npm scripts that invoke Stage4 macro execution does not need stage0 haxe to *build* or *select* a macro host\n- CI/Gate runners document expected macro-host provenance (prebuilt vs built)\n- Keep npm test green

Add a Stage3 diagnostic mode that executes macros + hooks and runs the typer over the full resolved module graph, but skips OCaml emission/build.

This lets us iterate Stage4 macro execution model and Stage3 typer coverage for upstream Gate1 without immediately being blocked by the bootstrap emitter's limited codegen.

  - `stage3=no_emit_ok`
- Command exits 0 and does not produce an `out.exe`.
close_reason: Implemented

title: hih native frontend: extend protocol to carry statement bodies
description: Protocol v1 only transmits method summaries (signature + first-return hints), which prevents Stage3 from emitting full OCaml bodies when using the native frontend.\n\nWe currently work around this for bring-up via HIH_FORCE_HX_PARSER=1 (pure-Haxe parser) when --hxhx-emit-full-bodies is enabled, but that won't scale to upstream modules that the pure parser cannot yet parse.
design: Add a backward-compatible protocol extension (prefer bumping to v=2) that can transmit a minimal statement AST for function bodies. Keep the subset aligned with HxStmt/HxExpr (SBlock/SVar/SIf/SExpr/SReturn/SReturnVoid + basic Expr forms like call/field/binop/unop/literals/ident).\n\nDecoding should be best-effort: unknown stmt/expr forms map to EUnsupported so the pipeline can keep progressing.
acceptance_criteria: - Native parser can emit bodies for the minimal subset (at least SExpr(trace("HELLO");)).\n- ParserStage decoder rehydrates bodies into HxFunctionDecl.body.\n- Stage3 --hxhx-emit-full-bodies no longer needs HIH_FORCE_HX_PARSER for the subset (add a regression test).
close_reason: Implemented

comments.author: Marcelo Serpa
comments.text:

- std/runtime/HxHxNativeParser.ml now emits ast method_body records (payload: "<name>\n<bodySrc>").

- packages/hih-compiler/src/EmitterStage.hx now only treats locals as emit-safe when emitFullBodies=true (avoids unbound locals in return-only mode).
- Stage3 no longer auto-forces HIH_FORCE_HX_PARSER for --hxhx-emit-full-bodies; native protocol supplies bodies for the minimal subset.

Quality: npm test passes.

title: Gate1: upstream compile-macro: decide define compatibility for static-platform #if blocks
description:
Upstream unit tests contain many #if blocks like (flash||cpp||java||cs||hl) to detect "static platforms". OCaml target currently falls into the dynamic branch and hits typing errors (e.g. TestReflect null for Int).

Need a strategy for Gate1/Gate2: either (a) define an existing platform flag (e.g. hl) for upstream runs, (b) provide shims/compat defines, or (c) maintain a small upstream-compat patch set.

This should be documented and implemented in the runner scripts.
acceptance_criteria: - Strategy chosen and documented\n- Runner scripts updated\n- compile-macro suite compiles past static/nullability checks
notes: Decision: for Gate1 bring-up we do NOT spoof upstream platform defines (hl/cpp/...). Instead we keep the OCaml target portable surface permissive enough that the upstream dynamic-branch nullability checks typecheck and run. Documented in docs/02-user-guide/HAXE_IN_HAXE_ACCEPTANCE.md and noted in scripts/hxhx/run-upstream-unit-macro-ocaml.sh. Verified: npm run test:upstream:unit-macro-stage3-typeonly, npm run test:upstream:unit-macro-stage3-no-emit.
close_reason: Closed

title: hxhx(stage3): collapse return exprs that reference unknown value identifiers
description: Stage3 emitter currently attempts to emit return expressions that reference locals/fields/helpers (e.g. `b`, `tryNewBytes`, `untyped__...`) even though Stage3 does not model class fields or locals. This produces OCaml with unbound values. Treat any lowercase identifier in a return expression as poison unless it is a function parameter, and collapse such return expressions to the bring-up escape hatch (Obj.magic 0).
acceptance_criteria:
- scripts/test-hxhx-targets.sh passes
- Stage3 upstream compile-macro bring-up progresses past Bytes.ml unbound values like trynewBytes (next failure should be later)
close_reason: Stage3 now collapses return exprs that reference non-param value idents; upstream compile-macro bring-up emits/builds/runs successfully (still non-semantic).

title: hxhx(stage3): lex untyped/cast to avoid emitting bogus identifiers
description: Upstream-ish std code uses `untyped` (and sometimes `cast`) in return expressions. Stage3 lexer currently tokenizes these as identifiers, so emission can produce OCaml names like `untyped` and fail with Unbound value. Recognize them as keywords so the parser marks them unsupported and the Stage3 emitter collapses the whole return expression to Obj.magic.
acceptance_criteria:
- scripts/test-hxhx-targets.sh passes
- Stage3 upstream compile-macro bring-up no longer fails with Unbound value untyped
notes: Close note: Stage3 lexer now treats "untyped" and "cast" as keywords so return-expr parsing collapses those expressions instead of emitting an OCaml identifier named untyped.
close_reason: Lexer recognizes untyped/cast as keywords so Stage3 doesn't emit bogus  identifiers (upstream compile-macro now fails later)

title: hxhx(stage3): use ocamldep -sort for multi-module build order
description: Stage3 multi-module emit currently passes .ml units to ocamlopt in resolver order, which can put providers (Std, Sys, etc) after users and fail with OCaml error "Unbound module X". Run ocamldep -sort on emitted units to compute a dependency-respecting order, then link with the root module last to preserve main init ordering.
acceptance_criteria:
- scripts/test-hxhx-targets.sh passes
- Stage3 upstream compile-macro bring-up no longer fails with "Unbound module Std" due to unit ordering (next failure should be later)
close_reason: Stage3 build uses ocamldep -sort and emits a tiny Std shim; upstream compile-macro bring-up progresses past Unbound module Std (next failure: untyped)

title: hxhx(stage3): never throw on nested unsupported expressions
description: Stage3 emitter currently throws if an EUnsupported node appears inside a larger return expression tree (e.g. after partial parsing). In upstream-shaped code this aborts emission early (unsupported expression: ...). Make exprToOcaml treat EUnsupported (and ENull) as the bring-up escape hatch (Obj.magic 0) so compilation can progress to the next real failure.
acceptance_criteria:
- scripts/test-hxhx-targets.sh passes
- Stage3 upstream compile-macro attempt progresses past "unsupported expression" emitter failures (next failure should be a real OCaml compile error or missing mapping)
close_reason: Stage3 emitter no longer throws on partial unsupported/null exprs; upstream compile-macro bring-up now reaches real OCaml compile errors (e.g. module ordering)

title: hxhx(stage3): lex control-flow keywords to avoid bogus call emission
description: Stage3 return-expr parsing currently tokenizes control-flow words (if, else, switch, try, catch, etc) as identifiers. This can mis-parse return-if expressions as a call to ident "if" and emit OCaml like "if_ (...)". Teach the bootstrap lexer about these keywords so such expressions become EUnsupported and emit via bring-up fallback.
acceptance_criteria:
- scripts/test-hxhx-targets.sh passes
- Stage3 upstream compile-macro attempt no longer fails with OCaml error "Unbound value if_"
close_reason: Stage3 lexer recognizes control-flow keywords; upstream compile-macro bring-up no longer emits bogus if_ calls (next failure is deeper unsupported expr)

title: M10: Type.getClass (runtime class identity)
description:
Implement `Type.getClass(o)` for class instances by introducing a runtime class identity strategy that works with inheritance/interface upcasts (our OCaml representation uses `Obj.magic` for upcasts).

Requirements:
- `Type.getClass(o)` returns the most-derived class value when `o` is a class instance (and returns `null` for anonymous structures / non-class values).
- Works for values typed as a base class or interface but holding a derived instance.
- Integrates with existing `HxType` class values (`Type.getClassName(Type.getClass(o))` should match).
- Add portable fixtures + snapshot coverage.

Notes:
- This likely shares machinery with runtime RTTI/tagging for typed catches (bd: haxe.ocaml-3ta).
acceptance_criteria: Portable fixture covers: (1) Base-typed var holding Child -> Type.getClassName(Type.getClass(v)) is Child; (2) interface-typed var holding impl -> class name is impl; (3) anon object returns null; (4) dynamic edge-case documented.
close_reason: Closed

title: M10: type expressions / minimal Type API
description:

comments.author: Marcelo Serpa
comments.text:
Architecture checkpoint for Cpp DCE reflection class-literal seam.

Decision: keep the hf/nhf string overload as an intentional, narrow fallback boundary rather than removing it now. The primary C++ seam is typed call-site lowering: direct class literals passed to hf/nhf Class parameters render as Type::resolveClass("Path"), and smoke coverage asserts those calls do not pass std::string class names. The overload only covers degraded string-shaped carriers after inherited DCE helper metadata is unavailable; it immediately resolves the string back to a Class meta-value and forwards to the Class-valued helper.

title: R&D: scoped raw target-injection authority for low-level abstraction lanes
description: Research and design a narrow metadata-based authority island for raw target injection in haxe.ocaml, using the current haxe.go scoped raw-injection work as reference context rather than a blind copy. Compare the local OCaml lane/profile/boundary architecture and macro/runtime design against local haxe.go and reflaxe.rust enforcement models, then propose the OCaml-appropriate metadata shape, enforcement boundaries, and lane interaction. Carry over the rationale from haxe.go: raw target injection was restricted to avoid target-code sprawl and preserve analyzable contracts, but low-level abstraction modules still need an explicit escape hatch. Document the final tag with Why/What/How and explain exactly where it is allowed and why.
acceptance_criteria: 1) The task compares local haxe.ocaml architecture against local haxe.go and reflaxe.rust rather than treating the tag as copy-paste policy. 2) It records the haxe.go rationale for default restriction vs scoped low-level escape hatch. 3) It defines metadata name, lane/profile boundaries, and documentation requirements before implementation. 4) It states whether existing OCaml lane rules must continue rejecting raw target injection in any special scopes, or why that policy should change.
close_reason: Completed scoped OCaml raw-injection authority design. Compared local haxe.ocaml policy/enforcement against local haxe.go and reflaxe.rust: Go uses strict/example/metal gates plus @:goAllowRaw, Rust uses @:rustAllowRaw with metal cleanliness enforced separately, and OCaml has Stage0 StrictModeEnforcer plus Stage3 MetalProfileVerifier. Documented proposed metadata @:ocamlAllowRaw, allowed module/type scope, portable-only lane boundaries, documentation/test requirements, and explicit policy that metal and @:haxeMetal must continue rejecting raw __ocaml__. Updated docs index plus Dynamic/untyped, OCaml profile, and imperative-lowering docs. Validation PASS: git diff --check; npm run ci:guards. Artifact hygiene: docs-only seam, no bootstrap/heavy artifacts generated; repomix-output.txt left untouched. README Goals status table reviewed: no table change required because this is architecture/policy guidance and does not change production-readiness status for any main goal.

title: Narrow Dynamic usage in Stage3 backend dispatch
description:
Problem
- `Stage3Compiler.emitWithBackend` still uses `backendDyn:Dynamic` for bridge dispatch, which broadens an internal compiler API path.
- Repo policy forbids broad `Dynamic`/`Any` unless tightly justified at unavoidable runtime boundaries.

Goal
- Reduce `Dynamic` spread in Stage3 backend dispatch while preserving current behavior (including reflaxe bridge compatibility).

Scope
1) Refactor `emitWithBackend` to avoid broad `Dynamic` storage where possible.
2) Keep any unavoidable runtime-boundary cast isolated and documented.
3) Ensure existing backend dispatch behavior remains unchanged.
4) Keep docs updated if boundary policy wording changes.

Acceptance criteria
- `emitWithBackend` no longer stores `backend` as `Dynamic` for general dispatch.
- Bridge dispatch still works for current wrapper-backed backends.
- `test:m14:target-core-wiring`, `test:m14:backend-registry`, and `ci:guards` pass.
close_reason: Stage3 backend dispatch Dynamic scope narrowed; bridge behavior preserved.

  - kept `Dynamic` only at the final reflection fallback seam (`backendReflect`) where unavoidable

Validation

title: Narrow Dynamic usage in provider resolver helper
description:

- `BackendProviderResolver.requireProvider` still accepts `instance:Dynamic` even though the only behavior needed there is validating the `ITargetBackendProvider` contract and bridging to structural dispatch.
- The project rule forbids broad `Dynamic` usage except where narrowly justified at runtime boundaries.

Goal
- Reduce `Dynamic` scope in provider resolution by narrowing helper signatures to typed contracts while preserving current behavior.

Scope
1) Change `requireProvider` to accept a typed contract (`Null<ITargetBackendProvider>`) instead of `Dynamic`.
2) Keep constructor error handling unchanged in `registrationsForType`.
3) Keep the one scoped boundary cast (`return cast providerContract`) unchanged for now.
4) Update docs/comments only if behavior/contract wording changes.

Acceptance criteria
- `BackendProviderResolver` no longer takes `Dynamic` in `requireProvider`.
- Provider resolver integration tests remain green.
- `ci:guards` remains green (including provider boundary guard).
close_reason: Narrowed provider helper typing; dynamic boundary now downcast immediately in resolver path.

title: Provider boundary cast removal + typed provider registry hardening
description:
Problem
- `BackendProviderResolver.requireProvider` still uses a scoped boundary cast (`ITargetBackendProvider -> ProviderDispatch`) because OCaml bootstrap currently mis-lowers direct interface dispatch (`Unbound record field registrations`).
- We removed reflective static registration calls from the hot path, but dynamic provider loading still has one boundary conversion and should be revisited when interface-method OCaml emission is fixed.

Goal
- Remove or further constrain the remaining provider-boundary cast while preserving stage0/stage3 stability and deterministic provider precedence.
- Evaluate whether provider discovery can become fully compile-time typed for builtin providers without losing plugin flexibility.

Scope
1) Re-check interface-method dispatch codegen for `ITargetBackendProvider.registrations()` and attempt a no-cast path.
2) If no-cast is still impossible, keep cast in exactly one helper and add explicit CI guards preventing cast spread.
3) Evaluate provider registration strategies:
   - Option A: static provider table (`providerRegistrations` functions referenced directly at compile time).
   - Option B: macro-generated provider registry (compile-time discovery of known providers).
   - Option C: keep current mixed model (typed known-provider table + dynamic provider loading by type path).
4) Document recommendation with tradeoffs and chosen path.

Pros/Cons to assess
- Static provider table
  Pros: strongest compile-time typing, no reflection for known providers, simple runtime behavior.
  Cons: manual maintenance overhead when new builtin providers are added.
- Macro-generated registry
  Pros: compile-time typing with less manual table upkeep, central source of truth.
  Cons: added macro/build complexity, harder debugging when discovery fails, potential bootstrap coupling risk.
- Mixed model (current)
  Pros: pragmatic, supports plugins today, minimal churn.
  Cons: still has one boundary cast and dynamic edge cases.

Acceptance criteria
- Decision recorded in docs/bead comments with rationale and chosen strategy.
- If cast removed: stage0 build + provider integration tests pass.
- If cast retained: cast remains isolated to one boundary helper, CI guard enforces containment, and tests cover failure diagnostics.
- No broad `Dynamic`/`Any` regressions introduced in resolver/provider path.
close_reason: Cast retained as scoped boundary workaround; CI guardrail + docs + provider tests landed for mixed-model strategy.

comments.author: Marcelo Serpa
comments.text:
Decision summary
- Kept the provider-boundary cast in `BackendProviderResolver.requireProvider` as a scoped workaround.
- Chosen strategy remains mixed-model provider loading:
  1) compile-time known-provider table for bundled builtin providers,
  2) typed dynamic provider loading (`Type.resolveClass` + `Type.createInstance` + `Std.downcast(..., ITargetBackendProvider)`) for plugin/bundled providers.

Why this decision
- The OCaml bootstrap lane still needs one boundary cast for structural dispatch; removing it now regresses provider loading.
- Mixed model keeps deterministic fast-path behavior for builtins while preserving plugin flexibility without introducing macro-registry complexity.

Changes landed
- Added CI guardrail `scripts/ci/provider-boundary-check.js` and wired it into `npm run ci:guards`.
  - Enforces that provider-boundary cast usage stays isolated to `packages/hxhx/src/hxhx/BackendProviderResolver.hx`.
  - Enforces exactly one scoped `return cast providerContract;` occurrence in that file.
  - Blocks reintroduction of `Reflect.callMethod` in the provider-boundary resolver.
- Updated docs:
  - `docs/02-user-guide/HXHX_BUILTIN_BACKENDS.md`
  - `docs/02-user-guide/HXHX_BACKEND_LAYERING.md`
  to reflect typed dynamic providers + mixed-model decision and current cast policy.

Tradeoff evaluation recorded
- Static provider table:
  - Pros: strongest compile-time typing, straightforward runtime path.
  - Cons: manual maintenance cost as provider count grows.
- Macro-generated registry:
  - Pros: auto-discovery of known providers.
  - Cons: added macro/build complexity and bootstrap/debug coupling.
- Mixed model (chosen now):
  - Pros: practical balance for current scope, no additional macro infra needed.
  - Cons: one scoped cast remains until interface-dispatch codegen can be fully represented.

Validation
- `npm run -s test:m14:backend-provider-resolver`
- `npm run -s test:m14:backend-registry`
- `npm run ci:guards`

title: Review provider boundary cast in BackendProviderResolver
description:
Problem
- `BackendProviderResolver.requireProvider` currently returns `cast providerContract` (ITargetBackendProvider -> ProviderDispatch structural view).
- The cast was introduced to avoid OCaml bootstrap failure (`Unbound record field registrations`) when calling `provider.registrations()` through interface-typed dispatch.

Why this needs follow-up
- We need to verify whether this cast can be removed (or replaced with a compile-time-safe adapter) without regressing stage0 bootstrap compatibility.
- The cast sits on a correctness-critical backend/plugin boundary and should remain tightly scoped/documented if it stays.

Investigation scope
- Reproduce/confirm the OCaml failure mode for direct interface dispatch in this path.
- Evaluate alternatives:
  1) backend/runtime support for interface-method dispatch on this boundary,
  2) typed adapter/helper generated at compile time,
  3) structural-provider view without cast (if possible),
  4) keeping cast with stricter guardrails and tests.
- Ensure no fallback to broad `Dynamic`/reflection dispatch in resolver.

Acceptance criteria
- Decision documented in bead comments (keep vs remove cast) with rationale.
- If removed: stage0 `scripts/hxhx/build-hxhx.sh` succeeds and provider resolver tests stay green.
- If kept: cast remains isolated to one boundary helper with explicit docs + regression coverage proving guard behavior.
close_reason: Decision recorded: keep scoped provider-boundary cast for now; validated stage0 bootstrap + provider resolver + target gates after typed catch/ValueException fixes.

comments.author: Marcelo Serpa
comments.text:
Investigation summary
- Reproduced that direct interface dispatch from `ITargetBackendProvider` to `provider.registrations()` emits OCaml record-field access and fails in stage0 bootstrap (`Unbound record field registrations`).
- Confirmed the boundary cast is currently required to switch to structural dispatch (`ProviderDispatch`) while still validating contract via `Std.downcast(..., ITargetBackendProvider)`.

Additional fixes landed
- Added OCaml-target implementation for `haxe.ValueException` (`packages/reflaxe.ocaml/src/haxe/ValueException.cross.hx`).
- Added forced type loading for `haxe.ValueException` in OCaml compiler init so typed catch lowering links reliably (`packages/reflaxe.ocaml/src/reflaxe/ocaml/CompilerInit.hx`).
- Kept cast isolated to `BackendProviderResolver.requireProvider`.

Validation
- `HXHX_FORCE_STAGE0=1 scripts/hxhx/build-hxhx.sh`
- `npm run -s test:m14:backend-provider-resolver`
- `HXHX_BIN=packages/hxhx/out/_build/default/out.bc npm run -s test:hxhx-targets`
- `npm run ci:guards`

Decision
- Keep cast for now as a scoped boundary workaround; track true removal when interface-method OCaml emission is fixed.

title: Follow-up: strict typed provider dispatch in bootstrap
description:
Problem
- We attempted stricter typing in `hxhx.BackendProviderResolver` (typed catch and typed provider-interface dispatch), but stage0 bootstrap generation currently fails:
  - Typed catch `catch (error:haxe.Exception)` requires `Haxe_ValueException` in generated OCaml path (`Unbound module Haxe_ValueException`).
  - Direct interface dispatch `provider.registrations()` after `Std.downcast`/cast fails in generated OCaml (`Unbound record field registrations`).

Current state
- Resolver now keeps deterministic known-provider fast-path and dynamic provider validation via `Std.isOfType(instance, ITargetBackendProvider)`.
- Dynamic provider `registrations()` invocation uses reflection as a compatibility bridge.
- This keeps stage0 and hxhx-target gates green.

Follow-up goal
- Eliminate dynamic-catch and reflective registrations call once bootstrap/runtime supports typed exception wrapping and interface dispatch for this path.

Acceptance criteria
- Stage0 `build-hxhx.sh` succeeds with typed catch in resolver.
- Dynamic provider invocation compiles via typed `ITargetBackendProvider` call path (no `Reflect.callMethod` in resolver).
- Existing provider resolver tests + `test:hxhx-targets` stay green.
close_reason: Replaced reflective provider invocation with typed contract + structural dispatch bridge, switched resolver catch to haxe.Exception, and added ValueException keep path so stage0 bootstrap compile succeeds; validated with stage0 build, m14 resolver test, and test:hxhx-targets.

What
- Extend the native frontend protocol and its Haxe decoder so non-static `var` fields are available to TyperIndex/TyperStage.

How
- Add a new `ast field` record (or equivalent) carrying: name, visibility, static flag, type hint, optional init expr summary.
- Update packages/hih-compiler/src/ParserStage.hx decoder to ingest it into HxFieldDecl.
- Add a Stage3 regression fixture that uses `this.field` and requires correct typing/emission.
acceptance_criteria: - Stage3 typer can resolve and type this.x where x is declared as a non-static var\n- No regressions in npm test\n- Protocol changes are versioned/documented

notes: Starting with OCaml-native approach: emit OCaml line directives ("# 1 "file"") at module boundaries and optionally around expressions to improve compiler error locations; evaluate sourcemap JSON as follow-up.

title: Spike: family portable|metal consolidation alignment for hxhx/reflaxe.ocaml
description:
## Why
hxhx/reflaxe.ocaml already has strong profile and runtime-slicing foundations. This spike aligns it to the family contract and identifies where inference/reporting should be hardened.

## Inputs
- Existing OCaml profile/runtime references:
  - `docs/02-user-guide/OCAML_PROFILE_CONTRACT.md`
  - `packages/hxhx-core/src/backend/OcamlProfile.hx`
  - `packages/reflaxe.ocaml/src/reflaxe/ocaml/runtimegen/RuntimeCopier.hx`
  - `packages/hxhx-core/src/backend/ocaml/MetalProfileVerifier.hx`
- Family/canonical references from Go:
  - `../haxe.go/docs/portable-canonical-contract.md`
  - `../haxe.go/docs/phase2-roadmap.md`
  - `../haxe.go/docs/hxrt-selective-runtime.md`

## Spike Scope
1. Compare current OCaml profile/runtime model against family portable|metal contract.
2. Evaluate replacing brittle runtime inference paths with compiler-tracked feature usage where feasible.
3. Define required contract/report artifacts:
   - profile contract report
   - runtime plan report
4. Define migration-safe metal fallback diagnostics policy (where appropriate).

## Deliverables
- Spike doc with:
  - gap analysis
  - hardening plan
  - phased implementation checklist
- Follow-up beads tasks linked to `haxe.ocaml-8nv`.

## Future Follow-up Trigger
After `haxe.go` selective runtime + metal fallback implementation stabilizes, run a new GPT-5.2 Pro cross-repo spike (Go/Rust/Elixir/hxhx) and reconcile family spec.
close_reason: Closed

design: Likely approaches: (A) generate a dune library stanza that includes all emitted modules and build it before ocamlc -i, or (B) add dune rules to infer module interfaces using the same build context; ensure runtime modules are excluded unless explicitly requested.
acceptance_criteria: -D ocaml_mli=all generates .mli for all emitted non-runtime modules without requiring the user to artificially reference them, and the output dune build still succeeds.

title: Cpp strict: preserve Map carriers for arrow map literals
description: The strict C++ run now passes generic abstract underlying-carrier conversions and first fails in TestType.testOpArrow. Haxe arrow literals such as [1 => 2, 3 => 4] are typed as Map values, but generated C++ declares them as std::vector<std::pair<...>> and then emits map.get(...). The same mismatch appears for Int, String, and object keys. Preserve the typed Map carrier and construction contract without special-casing the upstream test or growing an inline runtime stub.
